[codex] ## Operating Context
[codex] 
[codex] This repository coordinates the deployment and development environment for the Budget Analyzer application, a reference microservices architecture used as an open source learning resource for AI-assisted development.
[codex] 
[codex] This project is designed for AI-assisted development. The containerized development environment lives in the sibling `../workspace` repository; that repo owns the devcontainer configuration.
[codex] 
[codex] The `ext-authz` Go service implementation lives in the sibling `../ext-authz`
[codex] repository. This orchestration repository owns its Kubernetes manifests, Istio
[codex] `ext_authz` wiring, NGINX integration, Redis ACL wiring, production image
[codex] policy, and deployment documentation.
[codex] 
[codex] The default debugging model is split across host and container:
[codex] - Tilt runs on the host machine
[codex] - AI agents run inside the container
[codex] - The container has shared workspace access and full `kubectl` access to the host-managed cluster
[codex] 
[codex] The agent container is inside the trusted local-development boundary. Local
[codex] workspace files, the local Kind kubeconfig and Kubernetes Secrets, generated
[codex] development TLS keys, and disposable local API-test credentials are not hidden
[codex] from the agent. Never expose staging or production kubeconfigs, cloud or
[codex] deployment credentials, user credentials, or session cookies to this
[codex] container, and never use an agent session to deploy or administer staging or
[codex] production. Before an in-container agent-authorized cluster mutation, require
[codex] the current context and referenced cluster to equal `kind-kind`, require a
[codex] loopback Kubernetes API endpoint, and require the `kind-control-plane` node.
[codex] Use `kind get clusters` only as an additional host-side check because the
[codex] container Docker daemon cannot enumerate the host-managed Kind cluster. For
[codex] the full boundary and API-test target checks, read
[codex] `docs/architecture/autonomous-ai-execution.md` before changing agent sandbox,
[codex] credential, Kubernetes-access, or autonomous execution behavior.
[codex] 
[codex] Production target is Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Free Tier on ARM64:
[codex] - Shape: `VM.Standard.A1.Flex`
[codex] - Capacity: 4 OCPUs, 24 GB RAM
[codex] - OS baseline: Ubuntu 22.04 Minimal
[codex] - Region baseline: Phoenix
[codex] - Deployment model: single-node, production-grade demo environment
[codex] 
[codex] Architecture implications:
[codex] - All container images must support `linux/arm64`
[codex] - Local Tilt/Kind and OCI/k3s are both treated as production-grade deployment paths
[codex] - Observability remains internal-only in both environments
[codex] 
[codex] Architecture principles:
[codex] - Production parity between local Tilt/Kind and OCI/k3s
[codex] - Microservices with clear service boundaries and independent deployability
[codex] - Session-based edge authorization for browser security and session management
[codex] - Istio ingress handles ext_authz and auth-path throttling; NGINX handles API routing, backend/API rate limiting, and load balancing
[codex] - Resource-based routing keeps the frontend decoupled from service topology
[codex] - Defense in depth across Istio ingress, Session Gateway or NGINX, and downstream services
[codex] - Kubernetes-native development uses Tilt live update so code changes reach running pods quickly while the full security stack stays active; see `docs/development/local-environment.md#live-development-pipeline`
[codex] 
[codex] Technology pattern:
[codex] - Frontend: React web application
[codex] - Backends: Spring Boot + Java + Gradle
[codex] - Browser auth edge: Session Gateway (Spring WebFlux)
[codex] - External authorization: `ext-authz` Go service
[codex] - Edge and routing: Istio ingress/egress plus NGINX API gateway
[codex] - Infrastructure: PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ
[codex] - Monitoring: Prometheus, Grafana, Jaeger, Kiali
[codex] 
[codex] Service topology summary:
[codex] - Frontend: React web application for browser clients
[codex] - Backend workloads: Spring Boot microservices behind NGINX, plus Session Gateway and `ext-authz` on the auth and authorization path
[codex] - Infrastructure: PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ in the `infrastructure` namespace; Redis `/data` is PVC-backed through the `redis-data` claim template
[codex] - Monitoring: Prometheus, Grafana, kube-state-metrics, the repo-managed Jaeger v2 backend, and standalone Kiali in `monitoring`; Jaeger and Kiali stay `ClusterIP`-only
[codex] - Ingress and egress: Istio ingress handles browser entry, `ext_authz`, and auth-path throttling; Istio egress stays `ClusterIP` with `REGISTRY_ONLY`
[codex] - Exact service ports and exposure rules live in `docs/architecture/port-reference.md`
[codex] 
[codex] Adding a new service:
[codex] - Create manifests in `kubernetes/services/{name}/`
[codex] - Register the service in `Tiltfile`
[codex] - Add NGINX routes when the service owns public resources
[codex] - See `docs/architecture/session-edge-authorization-pattern.md` and `nginx/README.md`
[codex] 
[codex] Version numbers and concrete dependency selections live in service repos, manifests, and checked-in release inputs, not in this file.
[codex]

[codex] ## Core Runtime Pattern
[codex] 
[codex] The primary request flow is:
[codex] 
[codex] ```text
[codex] Browser -> Istio Ingress -> ext_authz validates session -> NGINX -> services
[codex] Auth paths -> Istio Ingress -> Session Gateway
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] Entry-point ownership:
[codex] - Browser auth lifecycle stays on the direct Session Gateway lane
[codex] - API traffic stays on the NGINX lane with ingress-layer `ext_authz`
[codex] - Exact route ownership and `/api-docs` behavior live in `docs/architecture/session-edge-authorization-pattern.md` and `docs-aggregator/README.md`
[codex] 
[codex] Session and identity rules:
[codex] - Session Gateway resolves roles and permissions from `permission-service` during session creation and owns browser session lifecycle on the direct auth lane
[codex] - Keep browser session logic on the direct `/auth/*` lane rather than pushing it through the general API path
[codex] - Exact browser endpoints and the shared Session Gateway/`ext_authz` contract live in `docs/architecture/session-edge-authorization-pattern.md`
[codex] 
[codex] Operational guardrails:
[codex] - Follow the resource-based routing pattern for new API endpoints
[codex] - Treat any new public `/api/...` route as incomplete until both `nginx/nginx.k8s.conf` and `nginx/nginx.production.k8s.conf` claim it and verification proves it does not fall through to the SPA
[codex] - Keep Spring Boot workloads on the startup/readiness/liveness probe pattern used by the checked-in manifests
[codex] - Keep PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, and Redis on their repo-owned stateful deployment patterns
[codex] - Redis `/data` is PVC-backed. Do not treat pod replacement or `tilt down` as a Redis reset. Use `./scripts/ops/flush-redis.sh` for a logical reset, or recreate the cluster/runtime when a full clean state is required
[codex] 
[codex] Observability rules:
[codex] - Grafana, Prometheus, Jaeger, and Kiali are internal-only in both local Tilt and OCI/k3s
[codex] - Use loopback-only access for operators: raw `kubectl port-forward --address 127.0.0.1 ...` or `./scripts/ops/start-observability-port-forwards.sh`
[codex] - `./scripts/smoketest/verify-observability-port-forward-access.sh` is the focused access proof
[codex] - Do not introduce public observability hostnames
[codex] - Do not use `--address 0.0.0.0` for observability access
[codex] - Exact observability access commands, local ports, and Kiali auth flow live in `docs/architecture/observability.md`
[codex]

[codex] - The executable inventories live in `scripts/lib/image-pinning-targets.txt` and `scripts/lib/allowed-latest-image-refs.txt`
[codex] - Keep those inventories aligned with the static security guardrail checks
[codex] - Only the documented local image repos may remain on `:latest` in checked-in manifests
[codex] - Live Tilt deploys rewrite those same repos to immutable `:tilt-&lt;hash>` refs and currently force `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` on those managed deploys
[codex] - Treat every third-party `image:` or `FROM` ref as a digest-pinning target unless it is explicitly excluded in the inventories

[codex] ## Production-Grade Parity
[codex] 
[codex] Treat both supported runtime paths, local Tilt/Kind and OCI/k3s, as production-grade microservices deployments.
[codex] 
[codex] Do not present the following as durable fixes:
[codex] - manual live-cluster drift
[codex] - security bypasses
[codex] - relaxed policies
[codex] - untracked Helm overrides
[codex] - degraded persistence such as replacing StatefulSets with `emptyDir`
[codex] - orchestration-level compensations for service-owned defects
[codex] 
[codex] Temporary recovery commands are acceptable only when clearly labeled as diagnostics or incident-recovery steps. Every durable fix must be repo-owned, repeatable from scripts/manifests, documented in the affected runbook or plan, and verified with the relevant smoke or guardrail checks.

[codex] ## SSL/TLS Certificate Constraints
[codex] 
[codex] NEVER run SSL write operations from the AI container.
[codex] 
[codex] The container has its own `mkcert` CA, but the user's browser trusts the host CA. Certificates generated inside the container will cause browser trust failures.
[codex] 
[codex] Forbidden operations that must be run by the user on the host:
[codex] - `mkcert`
[codex] - `openssl genrsa`
[codex] - `openssl req -new`
[codex] - `openssl x509 -req`
[codex] - Any script that generates browser or infrastructure certificates, including `scripts/bootstrap/setup-k8s-tls.sh` and `scripts/bootstrap/setup-infra-tls.sh`
[codex] 
[codex] Allowed read-only operations:
[codex] - `openssl x509 -text -noout`
[codex] - `openssl verify`
[codex] - `kubectl get secret -o yaml`
[codex] - Certificate file reads for debugging
[codex] 
[codex] For live agent work against exactly
[codex] `https://app.budgetanalyzer.localhost`, agents may run the workspace-owned
[codex] `ensure-budget-analyzer-local-ca-trust` command to install the host-published
[codex] public root into container-local trust stores. Use
[codex] `check-budget-analyzer-local-ca-trust` for read-only trust diagnosis. Read
[codex] `../workspace/docs/local-budget-analyzer-tls.md` before changing or debugging
[codex] this flow.
[codex] 
[codex] If `nginx/certs/k8s/_mkcert-rootCA.pem` is missing, invalid, or stale, stop and
[codex] ask the user to run `./setup.sh` from the orchestration checkout on the host.
[codex] Do not generate or rotate certificates in-container, and do not bypass
[codex] verification with HTTP, `--insecure`, `verify=False`, or
[codex] `ignore_https_errors`.
[codex]

[codex] # Dependency Automation Plan
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Proposed; automation is not installed or enabled by this document.
[codex] 
[codex] Use Renovate to discover dependency updates and open reviewable pull requests across
[codex] Budget Analyzer. Keep GitHub Dependabot alerts enabled for vulnerability detection,
[codex] and use existing open-source scanners for dependencies that update discovery alone
[codex] cannot assess. No dependency upgrades are part of implementing this plan.
[codex] 
[codex] Preserve [the September 6 review](../research/dependency-update-review-2026-09-06.md)
[codex] unchanged as the acceptance benchmark. Its versions are historical observations,
[codex] not inputs to the bot's target selection. Automation must independently discover
[codex] equivalent or newer applicable updates. Record misses explicitly; an update PR is
[codex] not proof that the associated security advisory was detected.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Selected tools and cost
[codex] 
[codex] | Purpose | Selection | Cost and boundary |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | Version and digest update PRs | Open-source Renovate, run by the Mend Renovate Community GitHub App | The app explicitly supports public and private repositories without a paid plan. No self-hosted bot infrastructure is needed. |
[codex] | Dependency vulnerability alerts | GitHub dependency graph and Dependabot alerts | Available on GitHub Free. GitHub's hosted service is proprietary; the update engine and added scanning tools are open source. |
[codex] | Resolved Java dependency graph | Official `gradle/actions/dependency-submission` | Use the open-source `cache-provider: basic` path, not the proprietary enhanced cache or a preview subscription. |
[codex] | Image packages and vulnerabilities | Trivy CLI/action | Open source; no Aqua subscription, server, or commercial database required. |
[codex] | Frontend and Go verification | `npm audit` and `govulncheck` | Existing ecosystem tools; no subscription. |
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate is the sole update-PR owner. Do not add Dependabot version-update
[codex] configuration or enable overlapping Dependabot security-update PRs. Renovate can
[codex] consume Dependabot alerts and attempt security fixes itself. Alert-only findings,
[codex] especially inherited Gradle versions, remain visible when it cannot produce a fix.
[codex] 
[codex] The free Mend service currently documents unlimited repositories, one concurrent
[codex] job per organization, approximately four-hour scheduling for active repositories,
[codex] and a 30-minute job timeout. That is adequate for initial dependency discovery;
[codex] the pilot must verify actual completion for this project. Paid Merge Confidence,
[codex] enterprise scheduling, support, and approval for enhanced OSS resources are not
[codex] prerequisites.
[codex] 
[codex] GitHub Actions compute and artifact storage are a separate cost consideration.
[codex] Use standard Linux runners, short artifact retention, and existing jobs where
[codex] practical. Public-repository standard runners are free; private-repository usage
[codex] must fit the account's included allowance with paid overages disabled. Repository
[codex] visibility, billing settings, and bot installation cannot be inferred from the
[codex] checkout; the unauthenticated API check during planning returned HTTP 403.
[codex] Before activation, verify these settings. If a necessary capability requires a
[codex] subscription, trial conversion, paid runner, or additional spend, stop and discuss
[codex] it with the user. Do not silently switch to a paid offering or provision a server.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Scope and operating policy
[codex] 
[codex] The rollout covers `orchestration`, `service-common`, `currency-service`,
[codex] `permission-service`, `transaction-service`, `session-gateway`,
[codex] `budget-analyzer-web`, `ext-authz`, `workspace`, and
[codex] `budget-analyzer-api-tests`. Other sibling checkouts are outside this rollout.
[codex] Each sibling phase executes in that repository's context and reads its own
[codex] `AGENTS.md`; orchestration workers must not implement sibling service logic.
[codex] 
[codex] The implementation consists of repository configuration, small CI additions, and
[codex] documentation. Use native Renovate managers first. For existing shell variables,
[codex] Tilt strings, and download URLs, use Renovate's documented declarative regex
[codex] manager and annotation comments. This is configuration of an existing tool, not a
[codex] new dependency crawler. Do not build custom scanners, advisory matching code,
[codex] version-selection scripts, lifecycle services, dashboards, or cross-repo bots.
[codex] 
[codex] Put common rules in `renovate-presets/default.json` in orchestration. Sibling
[codex] `renovate.json` files extend
[codex] `github>budgetanalyzer/orchestration//renovate-presets/default`; keep file-specific
[codex] extraction rules in their owning repository. Publish the preset before activating
[codex] consumers. Documentation belongs in a future `docs/dependency-automation.md`,
[codex] with sibling docs linking to it instead of copying detailed policy.
[codex] 
[codex] Initial policy:
[codex] 
[codex] - Start from `config:recommended`, enable the Dependency Dashboard, and set
[codex]   `automerge: false` everywhere, including security fixes.
[codex] - Create routine PRs weekly, initially at most three open routine PRs per repo
[codex]   and two new routine PRs per hour. Security fixes bypass the routine schedule;
[codex]   verify the effective Renovate configuration preserves that behavior.
[codex] - Keep patch, minor, and major recommendations distinguishable. Show both
[codex]   maintained-line updates and later release lines where supported by the
[codex]   datasource. Use dashboard approval for majors and stateful/platform migrations;
[codex]   do not hide them using blanket major exclusions or restrictive version ceilings.
[codex] - Group only concrete compatibility families: React/React DOM, Vitest packages,
[codex]   related Spring coordinates within a repo, repeated Istio pins, and related
[codex]   chart/CLI declarations. Helm chart majors are not application majors: all
[codex]   controller/chart updates need review even when semver calls them a patch.
[codex] - Keep Helm 4, RabbitMQ/PostgreSQL migrations, and Kubernetes/Istio coordination
[codex]   visible as proposals requiring compatibility review. Bots cannot coordinate an
[codex]   atomic merge across repositories or infer the correct Spring release train.
[codex] - Enable digest refreshes and retain digest pinning and image flavor suffixes.
[codex]   Never replace an immutable reference with a floating tag. Verify ARM64 support
[codex]   before accepting image updates; an available registry tag is insufficient.
[codex] - Exclude historical docs, generated output, local `:tilt-*` images, and documented
[codex]   local image repositories from updates. First-party production artifact promotion
[codex]   remains owned by the existing release workflow and its synchronized manifest,
[codex]   inventory, and overlay; Renovate must not update those independently.
[codex] - New checks report the existing vulnerability backlog without blocking every
[codex]   unrelated PR. Publish findings and distinguish scan failures from findings;
[codex]   do not swallow authentication, database-download, or dependency-resolution
[codex]   failures. Introducing a vulnerability merge gate is a separate decision.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Coverage contract
[codex] 
[codex] Create an ordinary Markdown coverage report during implementation at
[codex] `docs/research/dependency-automation-coverage.md`. It records source paths,
[codex] extracted package identities, observed bot/scanner outputs, and remaining gaps.
[codex] Do not maintain a second hand-curated table of desired dependency versions.
[codex] 
[codex] | Baseline area | Automated update discovery | Security/support proof and expected limits |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | Spring Boot, Cloud, Modulith, SpringDoc, Testcontainers, other Java dependencies | Renovate Gradle/version-catalog and wrapper managers in all five Java repos | Submit resolved graphs, including Framework, Security, Jackson, Tomcat and Netty, to Dependabot. A Boot PR alone does not establish that its BOM fixes every finding. Overrides require service-owner assessment. |
[codex] | Frontend direct and transitive packages; later toolchain majors | Renovate npm manager, lockfile maintenance, Dockerfile and Actions managers | Dependabot alerts plus full and production-only `npm audit`. Compare advisory/package identities, not the old total of 20 findings. Preserve browser/SSR/dev-server applicability distinctions. |
[codex] | go-redis and Go runtime | Renovate gomod, Dockerfile, Actions, and workspace download extraction | `govulncheck ./...` must reproduce or explain GO-2025-3540 and distinguish reachable calls from package presence. |
[codex] | Redis, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, NGINX, Temurin, Jaeger, Swagger UI and other deployed third-party images | Dockerfile/Kubernetes/Helm-values managers plus Tilt and script extraction; digest updates | Trivy scans the exact selected digest and inventories the embedded software. A new digest does not prove the exact Redis or JDK patch or advisory fix. Missing package identification is a coverage gap. |
[codex] | External Secrets, Kyverno, cert-manager, Istio, kube-prometheus-stack, Kiali | Helm datasource mapped to shell and Tilt pins; explicit chart names and registry URLs | Render selected charts and scan their actual image refs. Chart versions differ from app versions. Controller advisories may lack matching image-package metadata and must be recorded as misses. |
[codex] | Prometheus, Grafana, Prometheus Operator, kube-state-metrics | Helm-values image refs plus chart updates | Scan explicitly overridden images as well as chart defaults. Updating a chart does not update an independently overridden image tag. |
[codex] | K3s, Kind binary/node image, Kubernetes tooling, Gateway API, Calico, Helm, Tilt and other pinned tools | Built-in Docker/release datasources and annotated existing pins | Show supported-line patches and newer releases independently. Tool versions coupled to checked-in checksums need complete checksum changes before merge. Pod Security labels are compatibility settings, not ordinary package pins. |
[codex] | Workspace base image, Node/Go, Zulu and installed packages | Dockerfile/ARG/download extraction where versions are declared | Scan a built workspace image for installed versions. Unversioned apt installs receive updates through rebuilds; Renovate cannot open a version PR for an absent patch pin. Preserve the digest-only Ubuntu base constraint. |
[codex] | GitHub Actions and Python API-test dependencies | Native Actions and Python managers where constraints/lockfiles permit updates | Unbounded Python requirements are not version pins. Report their detection and installed-environment audit coverage without pretending an unbounded spec can receive routine version bumps. |
[codex] | EOL decisions: Boot, Node, Go, RabbitMQ, NGINX, Kubernetes/K3s and Istio | Newer releases should be visible in the bot dashboard | Renovate release discovery, abandonment heuristics, and vulnerability scanners are not a comprehensive EOL detector. Retain a quarterly human support-policy check against upstream lifecycle sources. |
[codex] 
[codex] Both patch and major proposals must remain visible for broad tags such as
[codex] `redis:7-alpine` and `eclipse-temurin:25-jre-alpine`. Test actual extraction and
[codex] lookup: broad tags can produce only digest updates and conceal patch identities.
[codex] If a same-digest, explicit-version alias is needed for reliable recommendations,
[codex] record that as a separately reviewed representation change; do not silently
[codex] upgrade the underlying image during onboarding.
[codex] 
[codex] Keep tool versions with checksum tables, chart/application coupling, and the
[codex] digest-only workspace base behind dashboard approval until a proposal contains
[codex] all required companion changes. Use existing Renovate checksum capabilities where
[codex] they fit and verify them; regex extraction alone does not calculate arbitrary
[codex] checksums. Otherwise identify the missing companion work in the proposal and
[codex] retain existing validation failures. Do not weaken verification to make a bot PR
[codex] mergeable.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Acceptance and activation boundaries
[codex] 
[codex] The target is automated coverage of the same or a superset of the review's update
[codex] and security findings. Measure update discovery, advisory detection, and lifecycle
[codex] assessment separately. For every baseline item, record one of: reproduced,
[codex] superseded by a newer applicable finding, false positive with evidence, or missing.
[codex] Include the advisory identifier, affected package/version, proposed target where
[codex] available, output URL/artifact, and any required human compatibility decision.
[codex] 
[codex] All baseline areas must have a demonstrated extraction/scan path. Missing
[codex] high-priority findings block a claim of full review parity. Tool installation can
[codex] be reported complete while parity remains incomplete, but those are distinct
[codex] outcomes. If standard configuration and the selected tools cannot close a gap,
[codex] report it to the user; do not fabricate an advisory match, seed expected versions
[codex] into configuration, or add a custom implementation. The lifecycle and
[codex] exploitability limits above remain explicit even after successful onboarding.
[codex] 
[codex] Implementation phases prepare reviewable local files. No phase authorizes git
[codex] writes, merging dependency PRs, releases, certificate writes, or cluster changes.
[codex] The user owns committing and publishing changes. Before final observation, a
[codex] repository administrator installs the free Renovate App only on the scoped repos,
[codex] enables dependency graph and Dependabot alerts, grants the app alert-read access,
[codex] and confirms duplicate update-PR services are off. Prepare all configuration and
[codex] documentation before this activation handoff. Do not change GitHub settings while
[codex] merely executing this planning request.
[codex] 
[codex] Existing Maven package credentials are a prerequisite for complete Java graph
[codex] resolution and successful bot PR CI. Use the existing scoped GitHub Packages read
[codex] credentials in trusted CI, and Mend's supported encrypted credential/host-rule
[codex] configuration if Renovate needs private Maven lookup. Never put plaintext tokens
[codex] in presets or reports. Verify the free app supports the required authenticated
[codex] lookup before activation; do not replace it with Maven Local or drop internal
[codex] dependencies from the graph. Do not introduce privileged `pull_request_target`
[codex] execution of dependency branches to obtain secrets.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Execution runtime prerequisite
[codex] 
[codex] Before resuming this plan at Phase 2, the user will upgrade the sibling
[codex] `../workspace` sandbox from Node 22 to Node 24, update that repository's nearest
[codex] runtime documentation, rebuild the development container, and complete the
[codex] workspace-owned post-rebuild checks. This is a user-owned prerequisite, not a
[codex] dependency upgrade implemented by this plan. An orchestration worker must not edit
[codex] the workspace repository to satisfy it.
[codex] 
[codex] At the start of the next runner invocation, verify `node --version` reports major
[codex] version 24 and that `npm --version` succeeds. Stop if the rebuilt runtime is not
[codex] active. Renovate `44.65.5` previously loaded under Node `22.23.2` emitted an
[codex] unhandled `RegExp.escape is not a function` rejection while returning exit status
[codex] zero. Treat any uncaught exception, unhandled rejection, or fatal/error log from
[codex] Renovate as validation failure regardless of process status. After this prerequisite
[codex] is complete, run local Renovate validation directly under the workspace's Node 24;
[codex] do not hide a stale container behind an ad hoc downloaded Node runtime.
[codex] 
[codex] The manual Node 22-to-24 change becomes the declared baseline for later extraction
[codex] and image scanning. Record it as a prerequisite change, not as a Renovate-discovered
[codex] or bot-applied finding when comparing automation with the saved review.
[codex]

[codex] downgrades `full` dry runs to lookup; record GitHub-authenticated lookups and a true
[codex] GitHub-platform full dry run as explicit Phase 12 gaps rather than giving an agent a
[codex] token or blocking configuration preparation. Treat Renovate exceptions or error
[codex] logs as failures even if its exit status is zero. Run `bash -n` and `shellcheck` on
[codex] annotated shell files, actionlint on changed workflows, and the existing static
[codex] guardrails when their documented prerequisites are present. Missing local
[codex] prerequisites are blockers, not reasons to bypass checks.

[codex] # Scripts Directory
[codex] 
[codex] This directory contains automation for the Budget Analyzer orchestration
[codex] repository. Scripts are grouped by purpose so setup, validation, operational,
[codex] loadtest, and repository-management tasks have stable entry points.
[codex] 
[codex] This README is the canonical catalog for the `scripts/` tree and for
[codex] cross-cutting verifier entry points. The detailed OCI deployment operator
[codex] surface under `../deploy/scripts/` is owned by
[codex] [../deploy/README.md](../deploy/README.md); this file calls out only the deploy
[codex] commands that are part of the normal release or verification boundary.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Layout
[codex] 
[codex] ```
[codex] scripts/
[codex] ├── bootstrap/   # Host and cluster bootstrap helpers
[codex] ├── guardrails/  # CI-safe static security and manifest checks
[codex] ├── lib/         # Shared shell helpers and maintained inventories
[codex] ├── loadtest/    # Synthetic local fixture data helpers
[codex] ├── ops/         # Day-to-day local cluster operations
[codex] ├── repo/        # Cross-repository management helpers
[codex] └── smoketest/   # Local live-cluster validation gates
[codex] ```

[codex] ## Canonical Entry Points
[codex] 
[codex] - `../setup.sh` - Standard local platform bootstrap from the repository root.
[codex] - `bootstrap/check-tilt-prerequisites.sh` - Tooling and environment preflight.
[codex] - `smoketest/smoketest.sh` - Aggregate local validation sequence for a live
[codex]   Tilt cluster.
[codex] - `smoketest/verify-observability-port-forward-access.sh` - Focused
[codex]   loopback-only Grafana, Prometheus, Jaeger, and Kiali port-forward verifier.
[codex]   It defaults to the canonical `3300`, `9090`, `16686`, and `20001` local
[codex]   ports, starts any missing temporary forwards itself, reuses the expected
[codex]   existing loopback `kubectl port-forward` listeners on those canonical ports,
[codex]   and accepts flag overrides when some other intentional listener already
[codex]   owns one of them. It verifies Grafana health,
[codex]   Prometheus readiness, Jaeger query API access, Kiali UI shell access, and
[codex]   that unauthenticated Grafana and Kiali API access is rejected. Use the same
[codex]   loopback-only access model in local Tilt and production OCI/k3s for the
[codex]   observability components installed there, and do not use `--address 0.0.0.0`
[codex]   for observability access.
[codex] - `ops/start-observability-port-forwards.sh` - Foreground supervisor for the
[codex]   canonical loopback-only Grafana, Prometheus, Jaeger, and Kiali
[codex]   `kubectl port-forward` processes. It starts all four forwards by default,
[codex]   supports repeated `--component` selection plus per-component port overrides,
[codex]   prints the local URLs plus the Grafana password and Kiali token commands,
[codex]   and cleans up all child forwards on exit.
[codex] - `ops/triage-kiali-findings.sh` - Authenticates to Kiali, snapshots the
[codex]   current Kiali API findings plus recent Kiali warnings, compares them to live
[codex]   Kubernetes namespace object counts, and classifies the obvious buckets such
[codex]   as runtime-absent workloads, missing backend services, tracing dependency
[codex]   gaps, and likely low-signal waypoint warnings. Use
[codex]   `--runtime-shape production` on OCI so the helper expects the production
[codex]   frontend topology (`nginx-gateway` serves the bundle; no standalone
[codex]   `budget-analyzer-web` Deployment).
[codex] - `ops/show-pod-version-labels.sh` - Lists pod deployment metadata for the
[codex]   current Kubernetes context and warns when Budget Analyzer runtime pods do not
[codex]   match a schema v2 deployment manifest or the checked-in production image
[codex]   inventory. Use `--allow-mixed-deployment-id` for selective OCI rollouts where
[codex]   unchanged pods are allowed to retain an earlier deployment id. Use `--strict`
[codex]   when the warning check should fail the command.
[codex] - `ops/start-observability-ssh-tunnels.sh` - Workstation-side foreground SSH
[codex]   tunnel helper for production OCI/k3s observability access. It takes the OCI
[codex]   host as an optional argument or reads `OCI_INSTANCE_IP`, assumes `ubuntu`
[codex]   plus `~/.ssh/oci-budgetanalyzer`, opens loopback-only tunnels for the
[codex]   canonical Grafana, Prometheus, Jaeger, and Kiali ports, and expects the
[codex]   matching `ops/start-observability-port-forwards.sh` process to already be
[codex]   running on the OCI host.
[codex] - `ops/capture-prometheus-operator-baseline.sh` - Renders the upstream
[codex]   Prometheus stack without the repo post-renderer, extracts the operator RBAC
[codex]   objects, builds a representative `kubectl auth can-i` matrix for the
[codex]   operator service account, and refreshes the checked-in RBAC baseline note
[codex]   under `docs/research/`.
[codex] - `ops/post-render-prometheus-stack.sh` - Helm post-renderer for the
[codex]   Prometheus stack that replaces the upstream broad Prometheus Operator
[codex]   ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding with the repo-owned least-privilege split:
[codex]   one narrow cluster-read binding plus namespaced monitoring/default roles.
[codex] - `smoketest/verify-istio-tracing-config.sh` - Focused live-cluster verifier
[codex]   for the Jaeger OpenTelemetry extension provider and mesh-default Istio
[codex]   Telemetry resource.
[codex] - `smoketest/verify-monitoring-rendered-manifests.sh` - Renders the
[codex]   Prometheus stack and Kiali chart, then checks image pinning, service exposure,
[codex]   Kiali auth/RBAC posture, the exact approved Prometheus Operator
[codex]   namespace-scope args and effective RBAC model, and server dry-run compliance
[codex]   for rendered workload objects.
[codex] - `smoketest/verify-prometheus-operator-least-privilege.sh` - Full live
[codex]   verifier for the Prometheus Operator least-privilege posture. It reruns the
[codex]   rendered-manifest proof, checks the live operator RBAC object set, enforces
[codex]   the required positive and negative `kubectl auth can-i` matrix, reruns the
[codex]   monitoring runtime proof, and captures Kiali triage artifacts under `tmp/`.
[codex] - `guardrails/verify-static-security-manifests.sh` - Static manifest and
[codex]   security guardrail gate used by CI and local preflight.
[codex] - `guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` - Static verifier for the
[codex]   full Oracle production baseline: app overlay, production
[codex]   infrastructure overlay, production render output, and the production image
[codex]   Kyverno policy. It is non-mutating, but it requires a live
[codex]   `kubectl` context so the Kiali production render can use a Helm server-side
[codex]   dry run and capture the full namespace-scoped RBAC footprint.
[codex] - `../deploy/scripts/release/prepare-oci-manifest-from-current-stack.sh` - Normal
[codex]   local OCI desired-state preparation entry point. It validates clean source
[codex]   workspaces, compares current artifact source state with the production image
[codex]   inventory, previews tag actions for changed artifacts, creates and pushes
[codex]   missing source tags in `--push-tags` mode, then stops. After GitHub Actions
[codex]   publishes the expected GHCR tags, `--resolve-images` reads changed-artifact
[codex]   tags once, resolves digest-pinned refs, preserves unchanged artifact images,
[codex]   updates the checked-in production desired state, and stops for review.
[codex] - `../deploy/scripts/release/deploy-current-oci-manifest.sh` - Normal OCI-host apply
[codex]   entry point. It applies the checked-in production manifest, waits only for
[codex]   changed managed rollouts, and verifies live runtime metadata against that
[codex]   manifest.
[codex] - `../deploy/scripts/verify/oci-upgrade-lockstep.sh` - Non-mutating static
[codex]   verifier for OCI upgrade lockstep. It checks local Tilt chart pins against
[codex]   OCI version contracts; production deployment manifest, image inventory, app
[codex]   kustomization, runtime metadata patch, and release metadata agreement;
[codex]   production `/api-docs` render wiring; and digest-pin inputs for production
[codex]   infrastructure and Helm values.
[codex] - `repo/prepare-lockstep-release.sh` - Release-manager preflight for the
[codex]   lockstep source release. It validates the sibling repository set, prints the
[codex]   commit SHAs for the coordinated source state, verifies the
[codex]   `service-common` version contract, checks remote tag availability, and can
[codex]   prompt before delegating to `repo/tag-lockstep-release.sh`.
[codex] - `repo/prepare-service-release.sh` - Release-manager preflight for one
[codex]   runtime artifact. It validates only the selected artifact's source
[codex]   repository, prints the source commit, expected image tag, workflow page, and
[codex]   Java `serviceCommon` version when applicable, and can prompt before
[codex]   delegating to `repo/tag-release.sh --repo &lt;repo>`.
[codex] - `repo/tag-release.sh` - Normal single-repository release tag helper. It
[codex]   requires `--repo`, validates only that repository, and refuses tooling repos
[codex]   such as `checkstyle-config` for OCI runtime release tagging.
[codex] - `repo/tag-lockstep-release.sh` - Explicit helper for rare coordinated
[codex]   all-repo tags across the `LOCKSTEP_RELEASE_REPOS` set. Use
[codex]   `--repo-set runtime-images --current-state --plan-only` to preview which
[codex]   runtime image repos need the requested tag based on the current local HEADs,
[codex]   then rerun without `--plan-only` to tag only the missing repos and skip tags
[codex]   already pointing at current HEAD.
[codex] - `repo/generate-unified-api-docs.sh` - Regenerates the checked-in unified
[codex]   OpenAPI artifacts used by `/api-docs`.
[codex] - `repo/compare-test-coverage.py` - Compares committed coverage on every
[codex]   non-main core sibling repository with its local `origin/main` ref without
[codex]   switching branches or changing a working tree.

[codex] - `bootstrap/install-verified-tool.sh` installs repo-pinned `kubectl`, Helm,
[codex]   Tilt, `mkcert`, Kind, `kubeconform`, `kube-linter`, and `kyverno` releases
[codex]   after verifying checked-in SHA-256 values.
[codex] - `bootstrap/check-tilt-prerequisites.sh` validates local tools, pinned binary
[codex]   versions, the host-published public ingress CA, DNS, Docker/Kind
[codex]   prerequisites, inotify budgets, pinned Gateway API and Calico state, and
[codex]   optional runtime security state. It reports drift and install commands
[codex]   without performing interactive cluster changes.
[codex] - `bootstrap/check-infra-tls-secrets.sh` is the focused read-only post-check
[codex]   used by `setup.sh` and Tilt. Tilt reruns the host-only
[codex]   `bootstrap/setup-infra-tls.sh` before PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ start
[codex]   so namespace recreation cannot leave the infrastructure TLS secrets missing.
[codex] - `bootstrap/reconcile-kind-inotify-budget.sh` raises low Kind node inotify
[codex]   values used by Kubernetes log-follow streams. Tilt runs it as
[codex]   `kind-node-inotify-budget` on every `tilt up` before workload resources
[codex]   start.
[codex] - `bootstrap/install-calico.sh` installs or reconciles pinned Calico CNI for
[codex]   Kind clusters created with `disableDefaultCNI`. It also uses the inotify
[codex]   reconciliation helper. A live `docker exec kind-control-plane sysctl ...`
[codex]   recovery command is diagnostic only; use the helper or Tilt resource for the
[codex]   durable local fix.
[codex] - `bootstrap/setup-k8s-tls.sh` and `bootstrap/setup-infra-tls.sh` are host-only
[codex]   certificate bootstrap scripts. Do not run them from an AI container because
[codex]   the browser must trust the host mkcert CA. `setup-k8s-tls.sh` fails closed
[codex]   unless the target is the host `kind-kind` context backed by the `kind`
[codex]   cluster, then atomically publishes only the public mkcert root at
[codex]   `nginx/certs/k8s/_mkcert-rootCA.pem` for the workspace lazy-trust command.
[codex]   The publication remains ignored by Git; no CA private key is published.
[codex] 
[codex] Use `../setup.sh` when you want the full local bootstrap to converge
[codex] repo-managed prerequisites and recreate the local Kind cluster. Use
[codex] `bootstrap/install-verified-tool.sh` for a single pinned binary, and use
[codex] `bootstrap/check-tilt-prerequisites.sh` as a read-only report before or after
[codex] setup.

[codex] ## Ops
[codex] 
[codex] - `ops/render-istio-egress-config.sh` renders or applies the Auth0/FRED Istio
[codex]   egress manifests from `.env`.
[codex] - `ops/start-observability-port-forwards.sh` is the repo-owned convenience
[codex]   entry point for persistent local Grafana, Prometheus, Jaeger, and Kiali
[codex]   access. It keeps the forwards bound to `127.0.0.1` and tears them down on
[codex]   `Ctrl+C`. The focused smoke verifier remains the clean-shell proof path and
[codex]   coexists with that helper by reusing the expected canonical listeners
[codex]   when they are already running. Use explicit `--grafana-port`,
[codex]   `--prometheus-port`, `--jaeger-port`, and `--kiali-port` overrides only
[codex]   when some other intentional listener already owns one of those ports. If the
[codex]   helper reports a conflicting `code` listener on a canonical observability
[codex]   port, that is host-side VS Code port forwarding, not a repo-owned Tilt
[codex]   forward.
[codex] - `ops/triage-kiali-findings.sh` is the first-pass Kiali investigation helper.
[codex]   It reuses an existing loopback Kiali listener when one is already up, starts
[codex]   a temporary loopback-only Kiali port-forward when needed, authenticates with
[codex]   a short-lived `kubectl create token kiali` token, and prints a human-readable
[codex]   triage summary. It also compares the current Kiali findings against the
[codex]   expected app deployments in `default`, so it can say explicitly when cluster
[codex]   startup is the blocker and Kiali is just reporting missing runtime. Local
[codex]   Tilt defaults to the seven-workload topology; OCI production should use
[codex]   `--runtime-shape production` so the helper expects the six-workload topology
[codex]   where `nginx-gateway` serves the frontend bundle.
[codex]   It references [docs/runbooks/kiali-expected-warnings.md](../docs/runbooks/kiali-expected-warnings.md)
[codex]   for the warnings this repo intentionally ignores. Use `--output-dir &lt;dir>`
[codex]   when you want the raw JSON and log artifacts for later review.
[codex] - `ops/show-pod-version-labels.sh` prints all pods by default and marks
[codex]   Budget Analyzer runtime pods with `WARN` when deployment id, artifact
[codex]   version, source ref, source commit, service-common version, or image
[codex]   annotation differs from the expected schema v2 manifest/inventory metadata.
[codex]   Use `--deployment-manifest &lt;path>` for an explicit reviewed manifest,
[codex]   `--tracked-only` to hide third-party and infrastructure pods, and `--strict`
[codex]   to return non-zero on warnings. Use `--allow-mixed-deployment-id` when a
[codex]   selective OCI rollout should accept already-current pods from an earlier
[codex]   deployment id.
[codex] - `ops/start-observability-ssh-tunnels.sh` is the workstation-side companion
[codex]   for production OCI/k3s. First start the Kubernetes port-forwards on the OCI
[codex]   host, then from the workstation run
[codex]   `./scripts/ops/start-observability-ssh-tunnels.sh &lt;oci-host>` or set
[codex]   `OCI_INSTANCE_IP` and run `./scripts/ops/start-observability-ssh-tunnels.sh`.
[codex]   The helper keeps one SSH session open with local loopback tunnels for
[codex]   `3300`, `9090`, `16686`, and `20001`, and fails fast if the remote loopback
[codex]   endpoints are not reachable.
[codex] - `ops/capture-prometheus-operator-baseline.sh` is the repo-owned upstream
[codex]   comparison capture for the Prometheus Operator. It refreshes the chart
[codex]   render without the repo post-renderer, records the rendered operator RBAC
[codex]   plus a representative `kubectl auth can-i` matrix for
[codex]   `system:serviceaccount:monitoring:prometheus-stack-kube-prom-operator`, and
[codex]   rewrites `docs/research/prometheus-operator-rbac-baseline.md`. Run
[codex]   `smoketest/verify-monitoring-runtime.sh` separately after Tilt is up when
[codex]   you want the live runtime proof.
[codex] - `ops/post-render-prometheus-stack.sh` is the repo-owned RBAC reduction layer
[codex]   for `kube-prometheus-stack`. Local Tilt and production Helm installs both run
[codex]   through it so the Prometheus Operator loses cluster-wide `secrets`,
[codex]   `configmaps`, service mutation, and pod-delete authority outside
[codex]   `monitoring` while retaining the documented cluster-read exceptions for
[codex]   `namespaces`, `nodes`, `ingresses`, and `storageclasses`.
[codex] - `deploy/scripts/verify/network-policy-enforcement.sh` can run before
[codex]   production Auth0 config exists, but in that pre-Auth0 state the two positive
[codex]   `istio-egress-gateway:443` checks are deferred until the real egress routing
[codex]   is rendered and applied later in the production plan.
[codex] - `ops/grafana-ui-playwright-debug.sh` creates an ignored temporary Playwright

[codex] ## Loadtest Fixtures
[codex] 
[codex] Track 1 loadtest support is synthetic fixture data only. It creates local users,
[codex] sessions, and transactions for workflows like user deactivation and session
[codex] revocation without driving traffic.

[codex] 
[codex] # Later, when finished with the fixture set
[codex] ./scripts/loadtest/teardown-loadtest.sh
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] `seed-loadtest-users.sh` writes `.loadtest/session-pool.txt`, which is
[codex] gitignored and reserved for future traffic-replay tooling. The shared
[codex] `lib/loadtest-common.sh` helper resolves that pool path from the orchestration
[codex] repo root, so callers can run the loadtest scripts from any current working
[codex] directory without writing outside the repository.

[codex] # Dependency Automation
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Configuration prepared; administrator activation is still required.
[codex] 
[codex] This document owns the operating policy for dependency automation across the
[codex] Budget Analyzer repositories. The preserved
[codex] [September 6 dependency review](research/dependency-update-review-2026-09-06.md)
[codex] is the historical acceptance benchmark; its observed versions are not bot
[codex] targets. The executable rollout and acceptance sequence remains in the
[codex] [dependency automation plan](plans/dependency-automation-plan.md).
[codex] 
[codex] ## Ownership and policy
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate is the only service allowed to open dependency update pull requests.
[codex] Dependabot remains alert-only: keep the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts
[codex] enabled, disable Dependabot version updates and overlapping Dependabot security
[codex] update pull requests, and let Renovate consume alerts when its App permission
[codex] allows that. Never enable automerge, including for security fixes.
[codex] 
[codex] The shared policy is
[codex] [`renovate-presets/default.json`](../renovate-presets/default.json). Repository
[codex] configuration extends it and adds only repository-specific manager paths and
[codex] extraction rules. Routine pull requests are created weekly, with no more than
[codex] three open routine pull requests and two new routine pull requests per hour in
[codex] one repository. Vulnerability fixes use Renovate's dedicated alert path and an
[codex] unrestricted schedule. Major, chart, stateful, platform, and checksum-coupled
[codex] updates require Dependency Dashboard approval.
[codex] 
[codex] Patch, minor, and major proposals remain distinct. Digest refreshes must retain
[codex] an immutable digest and any image flavor suffix. Reviewers must independently
[codex] verify Linux ARM64 support. An available tag or a changed digest is not evidence
[codex] of architecture support, embedded package versions, vulnerability remediation,
[codex] or upstream support status.
[codex] 
[codex] The following stay outside Renovate ownership:
[codex] 
[codex] - historical/generated outputs and the retained stale test suites
[codex] - local `:latest` and generated `:tilt-*` images listed by the image-pinning
[codex]   inventories
[codex] - first-party production images and their synchronized manifest, inventory,
[codex]   overlay, runtime metadata, and API-docs metadata
[codex] - Pod Security compatibility labels
[codex] - arbitrary per-platform checksum calculation
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate may propose checksum-coupled tool versions, but dashboard approval and
[codex] the existing checksum verification remain mandatory. A reviewer must update the
[codex] complete checksum table; no validation may be weakened to merge the proposal.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Cost and service boundary
[codex] 
[codex] Use the open-source Renovate engine through the free Mend Renovate Community
[codex] GitHub App. Do not provision a self-hosted bot or opt into paid Merge Confidence,
[codex] enterprise scheduling, enhanced cache, a trial, or another subscription. The
[codex] selected security evidence uses GitHub's dependency graph and Dependabot alerts,
[codex] Gradle's open-source basic dependency-submission path, Trivy, `npm audit`, and
[codex] `govulncheck`.
[codex] 
[codex] GitHub Actions usage is separate from Mend hosting. Public repositories can use
[codex] standard hosted Linux runners. Before enabling automation for a private
[codex] repository, confirm its included Actions allowance and that paid overages are
[codex] disabled. Stop for user direction if required coverage needs spending or a
[codex] capability unavailable on the free offering.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Activation procedure
[codex] 
[codex] Configuration preparation does not authorize GitHub setting changes. A
[codex] repository administrator performs activation only after all rollout phases have
[codex] prepared and validated their files:
[codex] 
[codex] 1. Publish the orchestration repository and its shared preset before publishing
[codex]    consumer configurations.
[codex] 2. At the start of Phase 12, manually dispatch
[codex]    `dependency-automation-config.yml` with `run_hosted_dry_run` enabled. Its
[codex]    GitHub-provided job token has read permissions only, Renovate runs with
[codex]    `--dry-run=full`, and the user retains control of the trigger. Preserve the
[codex]    workflow URL and confirm that the published preset resolves before proceeding;
[codex]    never copy the job token into an agent environment.
[codex] 3. Confirm repository visibility, Actions billing/overage settings, and that the
[codex]    free Mend service supports every scoped repository and required authenticated
[codex]    Maven lookup within its job limits.
[codex] 4. Install the Renovate Community App only on the repositories listed in the
[codex]    rollout plan. Grant read access to Dependabot alerts when available.
[codex] 5. Enable the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts. Disable Dependabot version
[codex]    updates and automatic Dependabot security-update pull requests.
[codex] 6. Configure private Maven access only through Mend-supported encrypted secrets
[codex]    and host rules. Never commit a token and never use `pull_request_target` to
[codex]    expose trusted credentials to dependency branches.
[codex] 7. Run onboarding for orchestration first. Inspect the resolved configuration,
[codex]    extraction logs, dashboard, job duration, and any rate-limit or timeout
[codex]    message before enabling consumers.
[codex] 8. Record every baseline item in the coverage report as reproduced, superseded,
[codex]    false positive with evidence, or missing. Update discovery, advisory evidence,
[codex]    and lifecycle assessment are separate results.
[codex] 
[codex] The Community service's documented single concurrent organization job,
[codex] approximately four-hour scheduling, and 30-minute timeout are acceptable only if
[codex] the pilot completes in practice. A timeout or unsupported authenticated lookup
[codex] blocks broader activation; it is not a reason to omit dependencies.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Local validation and dry run
[codex] 
[codex] The focused workflow validates both JSON files with Renovate's official
[codex] `renovate-config-validator` under Node 24. Before publishing the preset, run the
[codex] same strict schema validation locally. For an unpublished-preset dry run, load
[codex] `renovate-presets/default.json` as the local self-hosted configuration, suppress
[codex] repository config discovery, and process the checkout with the local platform.
[codex] Use debug logging and do not provide a GitHub token or enable a write-capable
[codex] platform mode. Local mode proves extraction and supported lookups but does not
[codex] perform a true full dry run. Phase 12 owns the post-publication GitHub-platform
[codex] full dry run through the manually dispatched, read-only workflow; its ephemeral
[codex] job token is never provided to an agent.
[codex] 
[codex] Extraction and lookup evidence belongs in
[codex] [`docs/research/dependency-automation-coverage.md`](research/dependency-automation-coverage.md),
[codex] not in a second desired-version inventory.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Failure triage
[codex] 
[codex] - **Configuration error:** reproduce with the pinned validator version. Treat
[codex]   warnings and migrations as failures; correct the preset or repository config.
[codex] - **No extraction:** check the owning file's native manager pattern or adjacent
[codex]   annotation and compare debug logs. Do not seed the historical expected version
[codex]   into configuration.
[codex] - **No lookup or wrong package:** verify the real datasource identity, chart
[codex]   name, registry URL, tag prefix, build suffix, and flavor suffix. Record an
[codex]   unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.
[codex] - **Authentication or resolution failure:** preserve the failure. Fix encrypted
[codex]   Maven/registry access in the supported trust boundary; do not use Maven Local,
[codex]   drop internal dependencies, or swallow the error.
[codex] - **Finding without an update:** retain the Dependabot/scanner finding and route
[codex]   inherited or transitive remediation to the owning service. An update pull
[codex]   request is not proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] - **CI failure on a bot branch:** determine whether the proposal needs its
[codex]   documented checksum, chart rendering, ARM64, state migration, or cross-repo
[codex]   companion review. Do not relax a guardrail or create orchestration drift.
[codex] - **Scanner database/download failure:** report the job as failed separately
[codex]   from vulnerability findings. Never turn an unavailable scan into a clean result.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate discovery and vulnerability scanners do not comprehensively establish
[codex] end-of-life status. Owners must still perform a quarterly support-policy review
[codex] against upstream lifecycle sources.
[codex] # Dependency Automation Coverage
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Orchestration extraction pilot complete; hosted observation and
[codex] security-scanner phases remain pending.  
[codex] **Last updated:** 2026-09-06
[codex] 
[codex] This report records observed extraction and lookup behavior. It is not a list
[codex] of desired dependency versions. The preserved
[codex] [dependency review](dependency-update-review-2026-09-06.md) remains the
[codex] historical acceptance benchmark, and
[codex] [Dependency Automation](../dependency-automation.md) owns operating policy.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Pilot evidence
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate `44.65.5` was initially run under Node `24.13.0` and rerun under the
[codex] workspace baseline Node `24.20.0` against a plain copy of the checkout. The
[codex] unpublished shared preset and repository configuration were merged in memory,
[codex] repository config discovery was suppressed, and local platform dry-run mode
[codex] was used with debug logging. This avoids resolving the not-yet-published GitHub
[codex] preset and includes newly created, untracked files.
[codex] 
[codex] The final extraction rerun found 98 occurrences in 34 package files:
[codex] 
[codex] | Manager | Files | Occurrences | Evidence |
[codex] | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
[codex] | Dockerfile | 1 | 1 | `nginx/Dockerfile.prod-smoke-assets` -> `alpine` |
[codex] | GitHub Actions | 3 | 11 | Both existing workflows plus the new validator workflow; checkout, setup-node, Node input, and runner identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Helm values | 2 | 13 | Kyverno digest overrides and five kube-prometheus-stack image identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Kubernetes | 11 | 29 | Stateful infrastructure, Jaeger, service init images, gateway images, local first-party images, and Kubernetes API kinds were recognized. |
[codex] | Regex | 17 | 44 | Shell/Tilt chart pins, tool releases, Kind, Kiali, inline Temurin, probe images, Playwright, and the Renovate validator were recognized. |
[codex] 
[codex] Three of the GitHub Actions occurrences come from the manual hosted-dry-run job
[codex] and repeat already-covered runner, setup-node, and Node identities; they do not
[codex] add a new dependency surface.
[codex] 
[codex] The first lookup run completed in about 34 seconds and reported 57 distinct
[codex] dependency records, 31 outdated records, and 104 candidate branches before
[codex] routine limits and dashboard approvals. Live lookups succeeded for all six
[codex] configured Helm repositories, npm, and most container registries. The final
[codex] rerun completed lookup and returned 101 candidate branches, with the expected
[codex] missing-GitHub-token warning and an anonymous Docker token warning. Registry
[codex] lookup failures are retained below instead of being presented as a clean scan.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate's documented local platform supports `extract` and `lookup`, not a
[codex] true `full` dry run. Passing `--dry-run=full` falls back to lookup behavior.
[codex] Therefore extraction and live lookup are demonstrated locally, but branch-file
[codex] mutation and the published preset resolution still require a no-write hosted
[codex] observation after publication. No GitHub token was available in this worker,
[codex] by design, so GitHub-backed identities were extracted with
[codex] `github-token-required` and were not looked up. Those lookups are deferred to
[codex] the user-triggered Phase 12 job, which receives its ephemeral read-only token
[codex] inside GitHub Actions.

[codex] # Dependency Automation Coverage
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Orchestration extraction pilot complete; hosted observation and
[codex] security-scanner phases remain pending.  
[codex] **Last updated:** 2026-09-06
[codex] 
[codex] This report records observed extraction and lookup behavior. It is not a list
[codex] of desired dependency versions. The preserved
[codex] [dependency review](dependency-update-review-2026-09-06.md) remains the
[codex] historical acceptance benchmark, and
[codex] [Dependency Automation](../dependency-automation.md) owns operating policy.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Pilot evidence
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate `44.65.5` was initially run under Node `24.13.0` and rerun under the
[codex] workspace baseline Node `24.20.0` against a plain copy of the checkout. The
[codex] unpublished shared preset and repository configuration were merged in memory,
[codex] repository config discovery was suppressed, and local platform dry-run mode
[codex] was used with debug logging. This avoids resolving the not-yet-published GitHub
[codex] preset and includes newly created, untracked files.
[codex] 
[codex] The final extraction rerun found 98 occurrences in 34 package files:
[codex] 
[codex] | Manager | Files | Occurrences | Evidence |
[codex] | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
[codex] | Dockerfile | 1 | 1 | `nginx/Dockerfile.prod-smoke-assets` -> `alpine` |
[codex] | GitHub Actions | 3 | 11 | Both existing workflows plus the new validator workflow; checkout, setup-node, Node input, and runner identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Helm values | 2 | 13 | Kyverno digest overrides and five kube-prometheus-stack image identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Kubernetes | 11 | 29 | Stateful infrastructure, Jaeger, service init images, gateway images, local first-party images, and Kubernetes API kinds were recognized. |
[codex] | Regex | 17 | 44 | Shell/Tilt chart pins, tool releases, Kind, Kiali, inline Temurin, probe images, Playwright, and the Renovate validator were recognized. |
[codex] 
[codex] Three of the GitHub Actions occurrences come from the manual hosted-dry-run job
[codex] and repeat already-covered runner, setup-node, and Node identities; they do not
[codex] add a new dependency surface.
[codex] 
[codex] The first lookup run completed in about 34 seconds and reported 57 distinct
[codex] dependency records, 31 outdated records, and 104 candidate branches before
[codex] routine limits and dashboard approvals. Live lookups succeeded for all six
[codex] configured Helm repositories, npm, and most container registries. The final
[codex] rerun completed lookup and returned 101 candidate branches, with the expected
[codex] missing-GitHub-token warning and an anonymous Docker token warning. Registry
[codex] lookup failures are retained below instead of being presented as a clean scan.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate's documented local platform supports `extract` and `lookup`, not a
[codex] true `full` dry run. Passing `--dry-run=full` falls back to lookup behavior.
[codex] Therefore extraction and live lookup are demonstrated locally, but branch-file
[codex] mutation and the published preset resolution still require a no-write hosted
[codex] observation after publication. No GitHub token was available in this worker,
[codex] by design, so GitHub-backed identities were extracted with
[codex] `github-token-required` and were not looked up. Those lookups are deferred to
[codex] the user-triggered Phase 12 job, which receives its ephemeral read-only token
[codex] inside GitHub Actions.
[codex]

[codex]

[codex] ## Phase 2: Add exact-image security evidence
[codex] 
[codex] ### Workspace
[codex] 
[codex] .
[codex] 
[codex] ### Goal
[codex] 
[codex] Produce repeatable vulnerability reports for pinned infrastructure and controllers.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Scope
[codex] 
[codex] A standard Trivy workflow and the canonical documentation/coverage report.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Non-goals
[codex] 
[codex] No custom scanner, advisory correlator, persistent security service, or live cluster.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Required context
[codex] 
[codex] Read Phase 1 outputs, `scripts/README.md`, `kubernetes/production/README.md`,
[codex] observability values, and existing offline chart/render entry points. Identify
[codex] which existing render checks require a live API before selecting CI commands.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Execution steps
[codex] 
[codex] 1. Add weekly and manual scans of selected source refs. Reuse offline Helm and
[codex]    Kustomize rendering with the actual values and post-rendering configuration;
[codex]    collect image fields with standard YAML tooling and simple workflow steps.
[codex]    Include chart controllers, hooks and overridden monitoring images. Do not
[codex]    create a second handwritten list of image versions.
[codex] 2. Scan exact immutable image refs with Trivy for `linux/arm64`; include relevant
[codex]    local-only images on their actual platform. Save resolved ref/platform, package
[codex]    inventory, vulnerability report and scanner/database metadata as short-lived
[codex]    GitHub artifacts and summarize the findings in the job output.
[codex] 3. Include the Tilt Temurin base and standalone infrastructure images. Distinguish
[codex]    OS packages from embedded application versions; identify images Trivy cannot
[codex]    fully inventory. Do not infer a Java CPU or Redis patch from a tag alone.
[codex] 4. Report vulnerabilities without making the initial backlog a new merge gate.
[codex]    Make incomplete scans visibly fail and retain reports even when findings exist.
[codex]    Use CLI/artifacts without requiring paid private-repository SARIF hosting.
[codex] 
[codex] ### Implementation notes
[codex] 
[codex] Keep orchestration thin: native tools and workflow glue only. Rendering must not
[codex] need production credentials or apply anything. If a controller image cannot be
[codex] rendered offline with current entry points, report that prerequisite instead of
[codex] adding a live-cluster dependency. Pin newly introduced scanner/action inputs per
[codex] repository policy and include them in Renovate discovery.
[codex]

[codex]

[codex] Temurin, External Secrets/Kyverno and monitoring images. Prove reports identify
[codex] exact artifacts and retain database/scan errors. Compare advisory IDs with the
[codex] review and record unsupported image metadata rather than declaring a clean scan.
[codex]

[codex]

[codex] accessible through standard CI outputs, with no new service or paid feature.

[codex] # Dependency Automation
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Configuration prepared; administrator activation is still required.
[codex] 
[codex] This document owns the operating policy for dependency automation across the
[codex] Budget Analyzer repositories. The preserved
[codex] [September 6 dependency review](research/dependency-update-review-2026-09-06.md)
[codex] is the historical acceptance benchmark; its observed versions are not bot
[codex] targets. The executable rollout and acceptance sequence remains in the
[codex] [dependency automation plan](plans/dependency-automation-plan.md).
[codex] 
[codex] ## Ownership and policy
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate is the only service allowed to open dependency update pull requests.
[codex] Dependabot remains alert-only: keep the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts
[codex] enabled, disable Dependabot version updates and overlapping Dependabot security
[codex] update pull requests, and let Renovate consume alerts when its App permission
[codex] allows that. Never enable automerge, including for security fixes.
[codex] 
[codex] The shared policy is
[codex] [`renovate-presets/default.json`](../renovate-presets/default.json). Repository
[codex] configuration extends it and adds only repository-specific manager paths and
[codex] extraction rules. Routine pull requests are created weekly, with no more than
[codex] three open routine pull requests and two new routine pull requests per hour in
[codex] one repository. Vulnerability fixes use Renovate's dedicated alert path and an
[codex] unrestricted schedule. Major, chart, stateful, platform, and checksum-coupled
[codex] updates require Dependency Dashboard approval.
[codex] 
[codex] Patch, minor, and major proposals remain distinct. Digest refreshes must retain
[codex] an immutable digest and any image flavor suffix. Reviewers must independently
[codex] verify Linux ARM64 support. An available tag or a changed digest is not evidence
[codex] of architecture support, embedded package versions, vulnerability remediation,
[codex] or upstream support status.
[codex] 
[codex] The following stay outside Renovate ownership:
[codex] 
[codex] - historical/generated outputs and the retained stale test suites
[codex] - local `:latest` and generated `:tilt-*` images listed by the image-pinning
[codex]   inventories
[codex] - first-party production images and their synchronized manifest, inventory,
[codex]   overlay, runtime metadata, and API-docs metadata
[codex] - Pod Security compatibility labels
[codex] - arbitrary per-platform checksum calculation
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate may propose checksum-coupled tool versions, but dashboard approval and
[codex] the existing checksum verification remain mandatory. A reviewer must update the
[codex] complete checksum table; no validation may be weakened to merge the proposal.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Cost and service boundary
[codex] 
[codex] Use the open-source Renovate engine through the free Mend Renovate Community
[codex] GitHub App. Do not provision a self-hosted bot or opt into paid Merge Confidence,
[codex] enterprise scheduling, enhanced cache, a trial, or another subscription. The
[codex] selected security evidence uses GitHub's dependency graph and Dependabot alerts,
[codex] Gradle's open-source basic dependency-submission path, Trivy, `npm audit`, and
[codex] `govulncheck`.
[codex] 
[codex] GitHub Actions usage is separate from Mend hosting. Public repositories can use
[codex] standard hosted Linux runners. Before enabling automation for a private
[codex] repository, confirm its included Actions allowance and that paid overages are
[codex] disabled. Stop for user direction if required coverage needs spending or a
[codex] capability unavailable on the free offering.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Activation procedure
[codex] 
[codex] Configuration preparation does not authorize GitHub setting changes. A
[codex] repository administrator performs activation only after all rollout phases have
[codex] prepared and validated their files:
[codex] 
[codex] 1. Publish the orchestration repository and its shared preset before publishing
[codex]    consumer configurations.
[codex] 2. At the start of Phase 12, manually dispatch
[codex]    `dependency-automation-config.yml` with `run_hosted_dry_run` enabled. Its
[codex]    GitHub-provided job token has read permissions only, Renovate runs with
[codex]    `--dry-run=full`, and the user retains control of the trigger. Preserve the
[codex]    workflow URL and confirm that the published preset resolves before proceeding;
[codex]    never copy the job token into an agent environment.
[codex] 3. Confirm repository visibility, Actions billing/overage settings, and that the
[codex]    free Mend service supports every scoped repository and required authenticated
[codex]    Maven lookup within its job limits.
[codex] 4. Install the Renovate Community App only on the repositories listed in the
[codex]    rollout plan. Grant read access to Dependabot alerts when available.
[codex] 5. Enable the dependency graph and Dependabot alerts. Disable Dependabot version
[codex]    updates and automatic Dependabot security-update pull requests.
[codex] 6. Configure private Maven access only through Mend-supported encrypted secrets
[codex]    and host rules. Never commit a token and never use `pull_request_target` to
[codex]    expose trusted credentials to dependency branches.
[codex] 7. Run onboarding for orchestration first. Inspect the resolved configuration,
[codex]    extraction logs, dashboard, job duration, and any rate-limit or timeout
[codex]    message before enabling consumers.
[codex] 8. Record every baseline item in the coverage report as reproduced, superseded,
[codex]    false positive with evidence, or missing. Update discovery, advisory evidence,
[codex]    and lifecycle assessment are separate results.
[codex] 
[codex] The Community service's documented single concurrent organization job,
[codex] approximately four-hour scheduling, and 30-minute timeout are acceptable only if
[codex] the pilot completes in practice. A timeout or unsupported authenticated lookup
[codex] blocks broader activation; it is not a reason to omit dependencies.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Local validation and dry run
[codex] 
[codex] The focused workflow validates both JSON files with Renovate's official
[codex] `renovate-config-validator` under Node 24. Before publishing the preset, run the
[codex] same strict schema validation locally. For an unpublished-preset dry run, load
[codex] `renovate-presets/default.json` as the local self-hosted configuration, suppress
[codex] repository config discovery, and process the checkout with the local platform.
[codex] Use debug logging and do not provide a GitHub token or enable a write-capable
[codex] platform mode. Local mode proves extraction and supported lookups but does not
[codex] perform a true full dry run. Phase 12 owns the post-publication GitHub-platform
[codex] full dry run through the manually dispatched, read-only workflow; its ephemeral
[codex] job token is never provided to an agent.
[codex] 
[codex] Extraction and lookup evidence belongs in
[codex] [`docs/research/dependency-automation-coverage.md`](research/dependency-automation-coverage.md),
[codex] not in a second desired-version inventory.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Failure triage
[codex] 
[codex] - **Configuration error:** reproduce with the pinned validator version. Treat
[codex]   warnings and migrations as failures; correct the preset or repository config.
[codex] - **No extraction:** check the owning file's native manager pattern or adjacent
[codex]   annotation and compare debug logs. Do not seed the historical expected version
[codex]   into configuration.
[codex] - **No lookup or wrong package:** verify the real datasource identity, chart
[codex]   name, registry URL, tag prefix, build suffix, and flavor suffix. Record an
[codex]   unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.
[codex] - **Authentication or resolution failure:** preserve the failure. Fix encrypted
[codex]   Maven/registry access in the supported trust boundary; do not use Maven Local,
[codex]   drop internal dependencies, or swallow the error.
[codex] - **Finding without an update:** retain the Dependabot/scanner finding and route
[codex]   inherited or transitive remediation to the owning service. An update pull
[codex]   request is not proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] - **CI failure on a bot branch:** determine whether the proposal needs its
[codex]   documented checksum, chart rendering, ARM64, state migration, or cross-repo
[codex]   companion review. Do not relax a guardrail or create orchestration drift.
[codex] - **Scanner database/download failure:** report the job as failed separately
[codex]   from vulnerability findings. Never turn an unavailable scan into a clean result.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate discovery and vulnerability scanners do not comprehensively establish
[codex] end-of-life status. Owners must still perform a quarterly support-policy review
[codex] against upstream lifecycle sources.
[codex]

[codex] 302:The edge gateway uses NGINX 1.29.4, and the 1.29 mainline is no longer
[codex] 303:supported. NGINX 1.30.4 was the stable line and 1.31.5 the mainline release at
[codex] 304-review time.
[codex] 305-
[codex] 306-Recommendation: select either stable 1.30.4 or mainline 1.31.5 and update the
[codex] 307-unprivileged image, configuration validation, security documentation, and
[codex] 308-routing smoke tests together.
