[codex] # Kyverno Policies
[codex] 
[codex] This directory holds the admission-policy baseline.
[codex] 
[codex] - `policies/*.yaml` contains the ClusterPolicies Tilt applies to the local cluster.
[codex] - `policies/production/` contains production-only policy variants. The production
[codex]   image overlay verifier applies `production/50-require-third-party-image-digests.yaml`
[codex]   against the rendered production app overlay to prove the production image path
[codex]   has no local Tilt image exceptions.
[codex] - `tests/pass/` contains fixtures that must be admitted or intentionally skipped
[codex]   by documented system exceptions.
[codex] - `tests/fail/` contains fixtures that must be rejected.
[codex] 
[codex] Run the local policy fixtures with:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] kyverno test kubernetes/kyverno/tests
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] The static security guardrail gate wraps those fixtures together with schema
[codex] validation for checked-in manifests and rendered production overlays,
[codex] `kube-linter`, and repo-specific guardrail scans:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] ./scripts/guardrails/verify-static-security-manifests.sh
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] That script stays under `scripts/guardrails/` because it is CI-safe. The
[codex] live-cluster runtime proof stays separate under
[codex] `./scripts/smoketest/verify-security-guardrails.sh`.
[codex] 
[codex] That static gate also generates a small Kyverno replay from
[codex] `scripts/lib/allowed-latest-image-refs.txt` so representative approved local
[codex] Tilt `:tilt-&lt;hash>` deploy refs are rechecked even if the checked-in fixtures
[codex] stop matching the live apply path.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Production Path
[codex] 
[codex] The OCI production path does not reuse the full local `policies/*.yaml`
[codex] directory verbatim. It keeps the shared `00` through `40` policies, but swaps
[codex] the local image-admission rule for the production-only variant under
[codex] `policies/production/`.
[codex] 
[codex] Use the checked-in operator surface for that path:
[codex] 
[codex] - `deploy/helm-values/kyverno.values.yaml` pins the production controller
[codex]   replica counts, runtime-hardening values, and immutable digests for every
[codex]   rendered Kyverno controller and hook image.
[codex] - `deploy/scripts/reconcile/install-kyverno.sh` installs the pinned chart
[codex]   version into the `kyverno` namespace with those reviewed values.
[codex] - `deploy/scripts/reconcile/apply-admission-policies.sh` runs
[codex]   `./scripts/guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` first, then applies:
[codex]   - `policies/00-smoke-disallow-privileged.yaml`
[codex]   - `policies/10-require-namespace-pod-security-labels.yaml`
[codex]   - `policies/20-require-workload-automount-disabled.yaml`
[codex]   - `policies/30-require-workload-security-context.yaml`
[codex]   - `policies/40-disallow-obvious-default-credentials.yaml`
[codex]   - `policies/production/50-require-third-party-image-digests.yaml`
[codex]   It then checks the live `phase7-require-third-party-image-digests` resource
[codex]   for the production-only rule name and fails if the local Tilt/latest
[codex]   exception rules are still present.
[codex] 
[codex] The production apply path intentionally does not apply
[codex] `policies/50-require-third-party-image-digests.yaml`. The shared local `50`
[codex] rule accepts the approved local `:latest` and `:tilt-&lt;hash>` exceptions needed
[codex] for Tilt, which must never be active on the OCI cluster.
[codex] 
[codex] Current exception boundaries are intentionally narrow:
[codex] 
[codex] - `istio-ingress` keeps service-account token automount enabled for the ingress
[codex]   gateway's mesh identity bootstrap.
[codex] - `cert-manager`, `external-secrets`, `istio-system`, `istio-ingress`,
[codex]   `istio-egress`, `kyverno`, `kube-system`, `kube-public`,
[codex]   `kube-node-lease`, and `local-path-storage` are excluded from the repo-owned
[codex]   workload baseline because those pods are chart-managed or cluster-managed
[codex]   rather than orchestration-managed.
[codex] - Labeled cert-manager HTTP-01 solver pods
[codex]   (`budgetanalyzer.io/cert-manager-http01-solver=true`) are excluded only from
[codex]   the container-level security-context rules that cert-manager's Gateway solver
[codex]   API cannot express. They still remain subject to namespace labels, pod-level
[codex]   seccomp, automount, and image-admission policy checks.
[codex] - The third-party image-digest rule skips fully mutated sidecar-injected Pod
[codex]   objects by checking for `sidecar.istio.io/status`, because the autogen
[codex]   controller rules already enforce the repo-owned images at the Deployment /
[codex]   StatefulSet level while Istio adds chart-managed containers during mutation.
[codex]   The direct Pod rule still covers non-meshed temporary probes, and the rule
[codex]   also retains a narrow allow-path for injected Istio data-plane container
[codex]   names when the injector surfaces the current non-digest proxy image form.
[codex] - The local-image exception applies only to the seven approved Tilt-built repos
[codex]   and only for `:latest` checked into manifests or immutable
[codex]   `:tilt-&lt;16 hex>` deploy tags for those same repos. The policy also accepts
[codex]   the equivalent `docker.io/library/...` local form, keeps
[codex]   `imagePullPolicy: Never` for checked-in `:latest` refs, and accepts the
[codex]   current Tilt-managed `IfNotPresent` rewrite for live `:tilt-&lt;hash>` deploys.
[codex] - Namespace Pod Security labels remain required for all non-excluded
[codex]   namespaces, including temporary verifier namespaces.
[codex]

[codex]     return 1

[codex]         return 0

[codex]     "${installer}" "${tool}" --install-dir "${STATIC_TOOLS_BIN}"

[codex] }

[codex] collect_schema_manifest_files() {

[codex] kind_is_allowed_missing_schema() {
[codex]     local kind
[codex] 
[codex]     kind="$1"
[codex]     for allowed_kind in "${KUBECONFORM_ALLOWED_MISSING_KINDS[@]}"; do
[codex]         if [[ "${allowed_kind}" == "${kind}" ]]; then
[codex]             return 0
[codex]         fi
[codex]     done
[codex] 
[codex]     return 1
[codex] }
[codex] 
[codex] run_kubeconform_for_files() {
[codex]     local subject="$1"
[codex]     shift
[codex]     local output_file
[codex]     local summary_line=""
[codex]     local kubeconform_rc=0
[codex]     local -a unexpected_lines=()
[codex]     local -a missing_kind_lines=()
[codex]     local line
[codex] 
[codex]     if (( $# == 0 )); then
[codex]         echo "ERROR: no files provided for ${subject} kubeconform validation" >&2
[codex]         exit 1
[codex]     fi
[codex] 
[codex]     output_file="$(mktemp)"
[codex]     if "${STATIC_TOOLS_BIN}/kubeconform" -strict -summary "$@" >"${output_file}" 2>&1; then
[codex]         :
[codex]     else
[codex]         kubeconform_rc=$?
[codex]     fi
[codex] 
[codex]     while IFS= read -r line; do
[codex]         if [[ "${line}" == Summary:* ]]; then
[codex]             summary_line="${line}"
[codex]             continue
[codex]         fi
[codex] 
[codex]         if [[ "${line}" == *"could not find schema for "* ]]; then
[codex]             local missing_kind="${line##*could not find schema for }"
[codex]             if kind_is_allowed_missing_schema "${missing_kind}"; then
[codex]                 missing_kind_lines+=("${missing_kind}")
[codex]                 continue
[codex]             fi
[codex]         fi
[codex] 
[codex]         if [[ -n "${line}" ]]; then
[codex]             unexpected_lines+=("${line}")
[codex]         fi
[codex]     done &lt; "${output_file}"
[codex] 
[codex]     rm -f "${output_file}"
[codex] 
[codex]     if (( ${#unexpected_lines[@]} > 0 )); then
[codex]         printf '%s kubeconform validation reported unexpected errors:\n' "${subject}" >&2
[codex]         printf '  - %s\n' "${unexpected_lines[@]}" >&2
[codex]         exit 1

[codex] # Documentation Ownership
[codex] 
[codex] **Status:** Active
[codex] **Purpose:** Define the canonical owner for recurring documentation topics so
[codex] exact operational detail lives in one place and non-owner docs summarize and
[codex] link instead of copying.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Rules
[codex] 
[codex] - One recurring topic should have one canonical owner.
[codex] - Non-owner docs may give a short summary, orientation paragraph, or diagram,
[codex]   but they should not own the full command sequence, table, or contract.
[codex] - When a topic changes, update the owner doc first, then update summaries,
[codex]   indexes, and cross-links that point to it.
[codex] - `docs/archive/` is historical reference only and does not own active
[codex]   implementation detail.
[codex] - If no existing owner fits a new recurring topic, choose one and update this
[codex]   file in the same change.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Exact Detail vs. Summary
[codex] 
[codex] In this repo, "exact detail" includes things such as:
[codex] 
[codex] - full startup and verifier sequences
[codex] - complete port tables
[codex] - observability access commands
[codex] - detailed route ownership lists
[codex] - detailed `/api-docs` behavior and output definitions
[codex] 
[codex] Those details should live in the owner doc. Non-owner docs can summarize the
[codex] shape of the topic and link outward.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Ownership Map
[codex] 
[codex] | Topic | Canonical owner | Rule for non-owner docs |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | Documentation ownership policy | [docs/OWNERSHIP.md](OWNERSHIP.md) | Link here instead of restating the full ownership map. |
[codex] | AI instructions and repo guardrails | [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) | Other docs may describe the repo, but agent instructions and repo-operating constraints belong there. |
[codex] | Reusable `AGENTS.md` authoring standard | [docs/agents-md-checkstyle.md](agents-md-checkstyle.md) | Link here instead of restating the pattern-based authoring rules. |
[codex] | Release/deployment operating model and terminology | [docs/ci-cd.md](ci-cd.md) | Deployment docs and runbooks may summarize the modes, but source tags, artifact versions, `service-common` versions, image digests, and desired-state manifest terminology belong there. |
[codex] | OCI release deployment checklist and run log template | [docs/runbooks/oci-release-deployment-checklist.md](runbooks/oci-release-deployment-checklist.md) | Link to the template instead of copying the evidence table into plans or deployment docs. |
[codex] | Dependency automation operating policy | [docs/dependency-automation.md](dependency-automation.md) | Keep activation, cost, bot ownership, and triage detail there; the rollout plan owns implementation phases and the preserved review remains the historical benchmark. |
[codex] | Supported local happy path | [docs/development/getting-started.md](development/getting-started.md) | Point readers there instead of repeating the full supported setup flow. |
[codex] | Local environment mechanics and live-update internals | [docs/development/local-environment.md](development/local-environment.md) | Keep implementation detail there; summarize elsewhere. |
[codex] | Host-published local ingress CA contract | [docs/development/local-environment.md](development/local-environment.md) | Setup and agent docs may name the published file and consumer command, but keep certificate publication, trust ownership, and troubleshooting detail here. |
[codex] | Autonomous agent execution and local credential trust boundary | [docs/architecture/autonomous-ai-execution.md](architecture/autonomous-ai-execution.md) | Plans and setup docs may summarize the boundary, but local-only agent authority, credential exposure assumptions, and production exclusions belong there. |
[codex] | Manual Tilt/Kind bootstrap internals | [docs/tilt-kind-setup-guide.md](tilt-kind-setup-guide.md) | Treat it as a manual/deep-dive reference, not a competing default path. |

[codex] | Security controls and layered posture | [docs/architecture/security-architecture.md](architecture/security-architecture.md) | Link there for detailed control rationale and layered defenses. |

[codex] | Observability access model and operator entry points | [docs/architecture/observability.md](architecture/observability.md) | Keep exact access posture and port-forward commands there. |
[codex] | Resource-routing authoring and NGINX route work | [nginx/README.md](../nginx/README.md) | Architecture docs may reference the pattern, but NGINX route authoring detail belongs there. |
[codex] | Local script catalog and verifier entry points | [scripts/README.md](../scripts/README.md) | Other docs may call out specific scripts, but the `scripts/` tree map and canonical verifier entry points belong there. |

[codex] | Unified API docs surface (`/api-docs`) | [docs-aggregator/README.md](../docs-aggregator/README.md) | Keep exact route behavior, generated outputs, and docs-surface details there. |
[codex] 
[codex] ## `AGENTS.md` Special Case
[codex] 
[codex] `AGENTS.md` is intentionally rich direct AI context. It is the canonical source
[codex] for repo guardrails, execution constraints, and orchestration-specific working
[codex] rules.
[codex] 
[codex] It is not the canonical owner for every exact operational detail it mentions.
[codex] When `AGENTS.md` references setup flows, ports, observability access, routing,
[codex] or `/api-docs` behavior, prefer a stable summary plus a pointer to the owner
[codex] doc above instead of maintaining a second full inventory there.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Maintenance Workflow
[codex] 
[codex] When a recurring topic changes:
[codex] 
[codex] 1. Update the canonical owner doc first.
[codex] 2. Update summaries, indexes, and cross-links that mention the topic.
[codex] 3. Remove or shorten any duplicated exact detail that now conflicts with the
[codex]    owner doc.
[codex] 4. If ownership changed, update this file in the same change.

[codex] README.md:13:**One set of manifests, two environments.** The Kubernetes manifests under `kubernetes/services/` are the same ones that run in production. The production overlay (`kubernetes/production/apps/`) patches in pinned image digests and removes `imagePullPolicy: Never` — that's it. Infrastructure (PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ) follows the same pattern: production reuses the shared baseline and patches only storage sizing. Everything else — service accounts, deployments, services, network policies, Istio security policies — is identical.
[codex] README.md-14-
[codex] README.md:15:**Live code reload inside a real Kubernetes cluster.** Edit a Spring Boot service or the React frontend locally, and Tilt syncs the change into a running pod in seconds. Java services get a recompiled JAR synced and process-restarted; the React frontend gets sub-second Vite HMR. Changes to the shared library (`service-common`) automatically cascade to all downstream services. This all happens while the full production stack stays active: Istio mTLS between services, network policies enforcing least-privilege pod communication, ext_authz session validation at the ingress, and Kyverno admission policies guarding workload security contexts.
[codex] README.md-16-
[codex] README.md-17-**AI agents can debug the full stack.** The development environment runs inside a sandboxed Docker container ([workspace](https://github.com/budgetanalyzer/workspace)) that has kubectl, helm, tilt, and host-network access to the Kind cluster. An AI coding agent operating in this container can inspect pods, read logs, restart deployments, run tests, and trace requests through the mesh — the same workflow a human operator would use, with no special tooling or adapters.
[codex] README.md-18-

[codex] ## Local validation and dry run
[codex] 
[codex] The focused workflow validates both JSON files with Renovate's official
[codex] `renovate-config-validator` under Node 24. Before publishing the preset, run the
[codex] same strict schema validation locally. For an unpublished-preset dry run, load
[codex] `renovate-presets/default.json` as the local self-hosted configuration, suppress
[codex] repository config discovery, and process the checkout with the local platform.
[codex] Use debug logging and do not provide a GitHub token or enable a write-capable
[codex] platform mode. Local mode proves extraction and supported lookups but does not
[codex] perform a true full dry run. Phase 12 owns the post-publication GitHub-platform
[codex] full dry run through the manually dispatched, read-only workflow; its ephemeral
[codex] job token is never provided to an agent.
[codex] 
[codex] Extraction and lookup evidence belongs in
[codex] [`docs/research/dependency-automation-coverage.md`](research/dependency-automation-coverage.md),
[codex] not in a second desired-version inventory.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Failure triage
[codex] 
[codex] - **Configuration error:** reproduce with the pinned validator version. Treat
[codex]   warnings and migrations as failures; correct the preset or repository config.
[codex] - **No extraction:** check the owning file's native manager pattern or adjacent
[codex]   annotation and compare debug logs. Do not seed the historical expected version
[codex]   into configuration.
[codex] - **No lookup or wrong package:** verify the real datasource identity, chart
[codex]   name, registry URL, tag prefix, build suffix, and flavor suffix. Record an
[codex]   unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.
[codex] - **Authentication or resolution failure:** preserve the failure. Fix encrypted
[codex]   Maven/registry access in the supported trust boundary; do not use Maven Local,
[codex]   drop internal dependencies, or swallow the error.
[codex] - **Finding without an update:** retain the Dependabot/scanner finding and route
[codex]   inherited or transitive remediation to the owning service. An update pull
[codex]   request is not proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] - **CI failure on a bot branch:** determine whether the proposal needs its
[codex]   documented checksum, chart rendering, ARM64, state migration, or cross-repo
[codex]   companion review. Do not relax a guardrail or create orchestration drift.
[codex] - **Scanner database/download failure:** report the job as failed separately
[codex]   from vulnerability findings. Never turn an unavailable scan into a clean result.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate discovery and vulnerability scanners do not comprehensively establish
[codex] end-of-life status. Owners must still perform a quarterly support-policy review
[codex] against upstream lifecycle sources.

[codex] ## Pilot evidence
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate `44.65.5` was initially run under Node `24.13.0` and rerun under the
[codex] workspace baseline Node `24.20.0` against a plain copy of the checkout. The
[codex] unpublished shared preset and repository configuration were merged in memory,
[codex] repository config discovery was suppressed, and local platform dry-run mode
[codex] was used with debug logging. This avoids resolving the not-yet-published GitHub
[codex] preset and includes newly created, untracked files.
[codex] 
[codex] The final extraction rerun found 98 occurrences in 34 package files:
[codex] 
[codex] | Manager | Files | Occurrences | Evidence |
[codex] | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
[codex] | Dockerfile | 1 | 1 | `nginx/Dockerfile.prod-smoke-assets` -> `alpine` |
[codex] | GitHub Actions | 3 | 11 | Both existing workflows plus the new validator workflow; checkout, setup-node, Node input, and runner identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Helm values | 2 | 13 | Kyverno digest overrides and five kube-prometheus-stack image identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Kubernetes | 11 | 29 | Stateful infrastructure, Jaeger, service init images, gateway images, local first-party images, and Kubernetes API kinds were recognized. |
[codex] | Regex | 17 | 44 | Shell/Tilt chart pins, tool releases, Kind, Kiali, inline Temurin, probe images, Playwright, and the Renovate validator were recognized. |
[codex] 
[codex] Three of the GitHub Actions occurrences come from the manual hosted-dry-run job
[codex] and repeat already-covered runner, setup-node, and Node identities; they do not
[codex] add a new dependency surface.
[codex] 
[codex] The first lookup run completed in about 34 seconds and reported 57 distinct
[codex] dependency records, 31 outdated records, and 104 candidate branches before
[codex] routine limits and dashboard approvals. Live lookups succeeded for all six
[codex] configured Helm repositories, npm, and most container registries. The final
[codex] rerun completed lookup and returned 101 candidate branches, with the expected
[codex] missing-GitHub-token warning and an anonymous Docker token warning. Registry
[codex] lookup failures are retained below instead of being presented as a clean scan.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate's documented local platform supports `extract` and `lookup`, not a
[codex] true `full` dry run. Passing `--dry-run=full` falls back to lookup behavior.
[codex] Therefore extraction and live lookup are demonstrated locally, but branch-file
[codex] mutation and the published preset resolution still require a no-write hosted
[codex] observation after publication. No GitHub token was available in this worker,
[codex] by design, so GitHub-backed identities were extracted with
[codex] `github-token-required` and were not looked up. Those lookups are deferred to
[codex] the user-triggered Phase 12 job, which receives its ephemeral read-only token
[codex] inside GitHub Actions.

[codex] # Dependency Update Review Baseline
[codex] 
[codex] **Date:** 2026-09-06  
[codex] **Status:** Point-in-time research  
[codex] **Purpose:** Preserve the manually researched dependency recommendations so
[codex] they can be compared with repository-owned Dependabot and Renovate findings
[codex] after that automation is enabled.
[codex] 
[codex] This is not a version contract or an implementation plan. Upstream current
[codex] versions will continue to change. Checked-in build files, manifests, version
[codex] catalogs, and `deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh` remain the sources of
[codex] truth for selected versions.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Executive Summary
[codex] 
[codex] The highest-priority work is not a blanket migration to every current major.
[codex] It is a security patch batch covering Redis, the Spring-managed dependency
[codex] stack, External Secrets Operator, Kyverno, the frontend dependency tree,
[codex] `go-redis`, the JDK runtime image, and selected observability components.
[codex] 
[codex] Several runtime lines are also unsupported or approaching end of support:
[codex] Spring Boot 3.5, Node.js 20, Go 1.24, RabbitMQ 3.13, NGINX 1.29, and production
[codex] Kubernetes/K3s 1.34. Those should be handled as explicit migration batches
[codex] rather than mixed into low-risk security patch updates.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Security And Maintenance Patch Recommendations
[codex] 
[codex] ### Redis Server
[codex] 
[codex] | Item | Finding |
[codex] | --- | --- |
[codex] | Checked-in reference | `redis:7-alpine@sha256:7aec734b...` |
[codex] | Version resolved from the digest | Redis 7.4.8, image created 2026-04-17 |
[codex] | Recommended supported-line patch | Redis 7.4.11 |
[codex] | Major migration status | Redis 8 exists, but is not required for support |
[codex] 
[codex] Redis 7.4.8 predates the May 2026 security release and is affected by multiple
[codex] authenticated memory-safety vulnerabilities, including a `RESTORE` command
[codex] issue that may lead to remote code execution. This has practical relevance to
[codex] the current ACL model: `session-gateway` and `redis-ops` receive `+@all`, while
[codex] the other service identities are substantially narrower.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: refresh the Redis 7.4 image to 7.4.11 before considering a
[codex] Redis 8 migration. Review whether `session-gateway` needs `+@all` or can use an
[codex] explicit command allowlist that excludes administrative commands such as
[codex] `RESTORE`.
[codex] 
[codex] Primary advisory:
[codex] [GHSA-c8h9-259x-jff4](https://github.com/redis/redis/security/advisories/GHSA-c8h9-259x-jff4).
[codex] 
[codex] ### Spring Boot-Managed Backend Stack
[codex] 
[codex] The checked-in Spring Boot 3.5.14 BOM resolves these notable components:
[codex] 
[codex] | Component | Boot 3.5.14 | Boot 3.5.16 | Security floor observed in this review |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- | --- |
[codex] | Spring Framework | 6.2.18 | 6.2.19 | 6.2.19 |
[codex] | Spring Security | 6.5.10 | 6.5.11 | No advisory found for 6.5.10 in the queried database |
[codex] | Jackson BOM | 2.21.2 | 2.21.4 | 2.21.4 |
[codex] | Netty | 4.1.132.Final | 4.1.135.Final | 4.1.137.Final |
[codex] | Embedded Tomcat | 10.1.54 | 10.1.55 | 10.1.58 |
[codex] 
[codex] Findings include:
[codex] 
[codex] - Spring Web 6.2.18 is affected by an `UriComponentsBuilder` SSRF advisory;
[codex]   6.2.19 contains the fix.
[codex] - Jackson 2.21.2 is affected by deserialization authorization and polymorphic
[codex]   type validation issues; the relevant 2.x fixes are present in 2.21.4.
[codex] - Netty 4.1.132 is affected by request-smuggling, decompression denial of
[codex]   service, CORS bypass, CRLF injection, and resource exhaustion advisories.
[codex] - Tomcat 10.1.54 is in the affected ranges for several authorization and
[codex]   authentication advisories. The newest reviewed fixes require 10.1.58.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: first move the coordinated Java repositories to Spring Boot
[codex] 3.5.16. Because its BOM still selects Netty 4.1.135 and Tomcat 10.1.55, assess
[codex] temporary managed-version overrides to Netty 4.1.137 and Tomcat 10.1.58. Keep
[codex] this patch batch separate from the Spring Boot 4 migration.
[codex] 
[codex] Applicability caveat: several Tomcat findings concern container-managed
[codex] FORM/DIGEST authentication, WebDAV, AJP, or direct HTTP/2 behavior that the
[codex] current services do not appear to use. The affected components are still in
[codex] the deployed classpath, so patching remains preferable to relying only on
[codex] configuration non-use. Netty is directly relevant to the reactive Session
[codex] Gateway and other WebFlux/WebClient paths.
[codex] 
[codex] Representative advisories:
[codex] 
[codex] - [Spring Framework SSRF](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7m2p-62gw-p8qq)
[codex] - [Tomcat security constraint bypass](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5m62-pw8w-7w9f)
[codex] - [Tomcat authentication bypass](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9xv2-5v5q-p794)
[codex] - [Netty request smuggling](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-38f8-5428-x5cv)
[codex] - [Netty CORS header issue](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8c42-7qj2-3j46)
[codex] - [Jackson polymorphic validation bypass](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-j3rv-43j4-c7qm)
[codex] 
[codex] ### External Secrets Operator
[codex] 
[codex] | Item | Finding |
[codex] | --- | --- |
[codex] | Checked-in chart | 2.2.0 |
[codex] | Minimum security target identified | 2.4.0 |
[codex] | Current chart at review time | 2.10.0 |
[codex] 
[codex] External Secrets 2.2.0 is affected by DNS-based secret exfiltration through
[codex] the v2 template engine and a namespace-isolation bypass in `CAProvider`
[codex] ConfigMap resolution. Because this controller handles production secrets and
[codex] has broad cluster authority, it belongs in the critical monitoring tier even
[codex] though it was omitted from the former notification guide.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: validate a direct move to the current 2.10.0 chart. Do not
[codex] remain below 2.4.0.
[codex] 
[codex] Advisories:
[codex] 
[codex] - [GHSA-r2pg-r6h7-crf3](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r2pg-r6h7-crf3)
[codex] - [GHSA-wv26-88m5-6h59](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wv26-88m5-6h59)

[codex] ### Kyverno
[codex] 
[codex] | Item | Finding |
[codex] | --- | --- |
[codex] | Checked-in chart/application | 3.8.0 / 1.18.0 |
[codex] | Minimum security target identified | Application 1.18.2 |
[codex] | Current chart/application at review time | 3.9.0 / 1.19.0 |
[codex] 
[codex] Kyverno 1.18.0 and 1.18.1 are affected by a critical cross-namespace resource
[codex] generation vulnerability in namespaced CEL policies. The current repository
[codex] does not define `NamespacedMutatingPolicy` or `NamespacedGeneratingPolicy`
[codex] resources, which reduces present exploitability, but the controller is a
[codex] privileged admission component.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: update the Helm chart and Kyverno CLI together to the 1.19.0
[codex] application line, then render and rerun the existing policy and security
[codex] guardrail tests.
[codex] 
[codex] Advisory:
[codex] [GHSA-79gf-7frw-68m9](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/security/advisories/GHSA-79gf-7frw-68m9).

[codex] ### Frontend Dependency Tree
[codex] 
[codex] `npm audit` against the checked-in lockfile reported 20 findings: 3 critical,
[codex] 13 high, 2 moderate, and 2 low. `npm audit --omit=dev` reported four high
[codex] findings associated with Axios, React Router, React Router DOM, and a
[codex] transitive Axios dependency.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommended patch batch:
[codex] 
[codex] | Package | Checked-in/locked baseline | Patch target at review time |
[codex] | --- | --- | --- |

[codex] | React Router / React Router DOM | 7.14.2 | 7.18.3 |
[codex] | Axios | 1.16.0 | 1.20.0 |
[codex] | Vite | 6.4.2 | 6.4.3 or a separately planned major |
[codex] | Vitest packages | 3.2.4 | 3.2.7 or a separately planned major |

[codex] versions of `form-data`, `brace-expansion`, `browserslist`, `flatted`,
[codex] `js-yaml`, `nanoid`, `picomatch`, and `ws` are selected.
[codex] 
[codex] Applicability caveats:
[codex] 
[codex] - The critical Vitest issue requires the Vitest UI server to be listening; it
[codex]   is a development-tool risk, not production browser code.
[codex] - The reviewed Vite 6.4.2 issue requires a network-exposed Windows dev server.
[codex]   The supported container path is Linux, but the patch is still low risk.
[codex] - Most React Router findings concern framework, SSR, manifest, or RSC modes.
[codex]   The application uses `BrowserRouter`, not those server modes. The open
[codex]   redirect advisory is the most relevant browser-side reason to update.
[codex] - React Server Component advisories do not apply because no
[codex]   `react-server-dom-*` package is installed. React 19.2.8 remains the sensible
[codex]   paired patch level.

[codex] ### ext-authz And go-redis
[codex] 
[codex] `govulncheck` found a reachable call path from `ext-authz` to GO-2025-3540 in
[codex] `github.com/redis/go-redis/v9` 9.7.0. The issue may cause out-of-order responses
[codex] when `CLIENT SETINFO` times out during connection establishment. The first
[codex] fixed version is 9.7.3; the current release at review time is 9.22.0.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: update within go-redis v9, rerun `go mod tidy`, `go test ./...`,
[codex] `govulncheck ./...`, and the shared session-contract verifiers.
[codex] 
[codex] Advisory: [GO-2025-3540](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2025-3540).

[codex] ### Istio
[codex] 
[codex] | Item | Finding |
[codex] | --- | --- |
[codex] | Checked-in release | 1.29.2 |
[codex] | Latest patch on selected line | 1.29.7 |
[codex] | Current minor at review time | 1.31.0 |
[codex] 
[codex] Istio 1.29.2 is affected by a medium-severity failure mode in which an
[codex] unresolved `BackendTLSPolicy` CA reference can cause sidecars to send upstream
[codex] traffic in plaintext. The repository does not currently define a
[codex] `BackendTLSPolicy`, so the advisory is not presently reachable through the
[codex] checked-in configuration.
[codex] 
[codex] Recommendation: take 1.29.7 as the minimum maintenance update and plan a move
[codex] to 1.30 or 1.31 with the Kubernetes, Gateway API, and Calico batch. Istio 1.29
[codex] is expected to leave support around the end of October 2026.

[codex] # setup-trivy
[codex] Set up your GitHub Actions workflow with a specific version of [Trivy](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy)
[codex] 
[codex] # Usage
[codex] ## Install the latest Trivy version
[codex] ```yaml
[codex] # ...
[codex] steps:
[codex]   - name: Install Trivy
[codex]     uses: aquasecurity/setup-trivy@e07451d2e059ed86c2870430ea286b3a9e0bf241
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] ## Install a specific Trivy version
[codex] ```yaml
[codex] # ...
[codex] steps:
[codex]   - name: Install Trivy
[codex]     uses: aquasecurity/setup-trivy@e07451d2e059ed86c2870430ea286b3a9e0bf241
[codex]     with:
[codex]       version: v0.68.2
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] ## Caching
[codex] `setup-trivy` uses `actions/cache` under the hood but requires less configuration settings. 
[codex] This caches the trivy binary so that next time you run, instead of downloading the binary it is loaded from the cache. This is *not* the same cache as other Trivy artifacts such as `trivy-db` and `trivy-java-db`.
[codex] 
[codex] The cache input is optional, and caching is turned off by default.
[codex] 
[codex] **Caching is not supported for empty and `latest` versions!**
[codex] 
[codex] ### Enable caching
[codex] If you want to enable caching for Linux and MacOS runners, set the `cache` input to `true` and specify the `version`.
[codex] 
[codex] ```yaml
[codex] steps:
[codex]   - name: Install Trivy
[codex]     uses: aquasecurity/setup-trivy@e07451d2e059ed86c2870430ea286b3a9e0bf241
[codex]     with:
[codex]       version: v0.68.2
[codex]       cache: true
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] ### Custom path to Trivy binary
[codex] `action/cache` doesn't support absolute `path` for Windows runners (see [here](https://github.com/actions/cache/issues/1455) for more details).
[codex] 
[codex] To enable caching for Windows runner or if you need to change the Trivy installation directory for other reasons - use `path` input.
[codex] 
[codex] **`setup-trivy` adds `trivy-bin` directory to avoid caching unnecessary files** 
[codex] 
[codex] ```yaml
[codex] steps:
[codex]   - name: Install Trivy
[codex]     uses: aquasecurity/setup-trivy@e07451d2e059ed86c2870430ea286b3a9e0bf241
[codex]     with:
[codex]       version: v0.68.2
[codex]       cache: true
[codex]       path: "./bins"
[codex] ```
[codex] 
[codex] > [!IMPORTANT]
[codex] > `path` must be a **literal** path. Shell variables (e.g. `$HOME`, `$RUNNER_TEMP`) and `~` are **not** expanded and will fail the action.
[codex] > Use a GitHub expression that is resolved before the step runs instead, or a relative path like `./bins`.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Install Trivy with non-default token
[codex] There are cases when `github.token` (default value for `actions/checkout`) contains an invalid token for `http://github.com`.
[codex] One of example for this when using GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES).
[codex] See more info in https://github.com/aquasecurity/setup-trivy/issues/10
[codex] 
[codex] To properly install Trivy, you need to populate `token` from a secret or another step (e.g. from https://github.com/actions/create-github-app-token)
[codex] 
[codex] ```yaml
[codex] steps:
[codex]   - name: Install Trivy
[codex]     uses: aquasecurity/setup-trivy@e07451d2e059ed86c2870430ea286b3a9e0bf241
[codex]     with:
[codex]       version: v0.68.2
[codex]       cache: true
[codex]       token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_PAT }}
[codex] ```
[codex]

[codex] +# Render the repository-owned image inputs used by exact-image security scans.
[codex] +

[codex] +

[codex] +
[codex] +OUTPUT_DIR=""
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM=""

[codex] +usage() {
[codex] +    cat &lt;&lt;'EOF'
[codex] +Usage: scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh --output-dir DIR [--local-platform PLATFORM]
[codex] +
[codex] +Renders the production Kustomize overlays and pinned controller charts without
[codex] +contacting a Kubernetes API. Helm values and observability post-renderers match
[codex] +the checked-in production install path. Local-only Kind and build-image sources
[codex] +are copied or extracted into a separate platform directory.
[codex] +
[codex] +PLATFORM uses the Trivy/Docker form linux/amd64 or linux/arm64. When omitted,
[codex] +the local platform is derived from uname.
[codex] +EOF
[codex] +}

[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +default_local_platform() {
[codex] +    local architecture
[codex] +
[codex] +    case "$(uname -m)" in
[codex] +        x86_64|amd64)
[codex] +            architecture="amd64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        arm64|aarch64)
[codex] +            architecture="arm64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unsupported local architecture: $(uname -m)"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +
[codex] +    printf 'linux/%s\n' "${architecture}"
[codex] +}
[codex] +

[codex] +            exit 0

[codex] +
[codex] +          target_index=0

[codex] +      - name: Extract rendered image references
[codex] +        uses: mikefarah/yq@e1d5d6eb36b8995bf29e5acb561659824dc47be3 # v4.53.6

[codex] +          cmd: |
[codex] +            set -eu
[codex] +            : > scan-work/raw-targets.tsv
[codex] +            for platform_dir in scan-work/rendered/linux-*; do
[codex] +              platform="linux/${platform_dir##*-}"
[codex] +              for manifest in "${platform_dir}"/*.yaml; do
[codex] +                source_path="${manifest#scan-work/rendered/}"
[codex] +                yq eval-all --no-doc --unwrapScalar '
[codex] +                  (
[codex] +                    .. | select(tag == "!!map") | .image? |
[codex] +                    select(tag == "!!str")
[codex] +                  ),
[codex] +                  (
[codex] +                    .. | select(tag == "!!seq") | .[] |
[codex] +                    select(

[codex] +                      test("^--(prometheus-config-reloader|acme-http01-solver-image)=")
[codex] +                    ) |
[codex] +                    sub("^--[^=]+="; "")
[codex] +                  )
[codex] +                ' "${manifest}" |
[codex] +                  while IFS= read -r image_ref; do
[codex] +                    case "${image_ref}" in
[codex] +                      ghcr.io/budgetanalyzer/*) continue ;;
[codex] +                    esac
[codex] +                    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "${source_path}" "${platform}" "${image_ref}"
[codex] +                  done
[codex] +              done
[codex] +            done
[codex] +            sort -u scan-work/raw-targets.tsv -o scan-work/raw-targets.tsv
[codex] +

[codex] +          jq -Rn '
[codex] +            [
[codex] +              inputs |

[codex] +              sources: (map(.source) | unique)

[codex] +#!/usr/bin/env bash
[codex] +# Render the repository-owned image inputs used by exact-image security scans.
[codex] +
[codex] +set -euo pipefail
[codex] +
[codex] +SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
[codex] +REPO_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
[codex] +
[codex] +# shellcheck source=deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh
[codex] +# shellcheck disable=SC1091 # The repository root is resolved above.
[codex] +. "${REPO_DIR}/deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh"
[codex] +
[codex] +OUTPUT_DIR=""
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM=""
[codex] +
[codex] +usage() {
[codex] +    cat &lt;&lt;'EOF'
[codex] +Usage: scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh --output-dir DIR [--local-platform PLATFORM]
[codex] +
[codex] +Renders the production Kustomize overlays and pinned controller charts without
[codex] +contacting a Kubernetes API. Helm values and observability post-renderers match
[codex] +the checked-in production install path. Local-only Kind and build-image sources
[codex] +are copied or extracted into a separate platform directory.
[codex] +
[codex] +PLATFORM uses the Trivy/Docker form linux/amd64 or linux/arm64. When omitted,
[codex] +the local platform is derived from uname.
[codex] +EOF
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +die() {
[codex] +    echo "ERROR: $*" >&2
[codex] +    exit 1
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +require_command() {
[codex] +    command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "required command not found: $1"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +default_local_platform() {
[codex] +    local architecture
[codex] +
[codex] +    case "$(uname -m)" in
[codex] +        x86_64|amd64)
[codex] +            architecture="amd64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        arm64|aarch64)
[codex] +            architecture="arm64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unsupported local architecture: $(uname -m)"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +
[codex] +    printf 'linux/%s\n' "${architecture}"
[codex] +}
[codex] +

[codex] +            target_hash="$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "${platform}" "${source_ref}" | sha256sum | cut -c1-12)"
[codex] +            target_dir="scan-work/evidence/$(printf '%03d' "${target_index}")-${target_hash}"
[codex] +            mkdir -p "${target_dir}"
[codex] +
[codex] +            if [[ "${source_ref}" == *@sha256:* ]]; then
[codex] +              source_pin="immutable"
[codex] +              declared_digest="${source_ref##*@}"
[codex] +            else
[codex] +              source_pin="mutable"
[codex] +              declared_digest=""
[codex] +            fi

[codex] +              --arg source_ref "${source_ref}" \

[codex] +              '{platform: $platform, source_ref: $source_ref, source_pin: $source_pin, sources: $sources}' \
[codex] +              > "${target_dir}/source.json"
[codex] +

[codex] +              2> "${target_dir}/registry-resolution.stderr"; then
[codex] +              jq -n --arg result registry-resolution-failed '{result: $result}' \
[codex] +                > "${target_dir}/status.json"

[codex] +                "${platform}" "${source_ref}" "${source_pin}" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
[codex] +              incomplete=1
[codex] +              continue
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +
[codex] +            os="${platform%/*}"
[codex] +            architecture="${platform#*/}"
[codex] +            if jq -e '.manifests | type == "array"' "${target_dir}/registry-manifest.json" >/dev/null; then
[codex] +              resolved_digest="$(jq -r \

[codex] +                --arg architecture "${architecture}" \
[codex] +                'first(.manifests[] | select(.platform.os == $os and .platform.architecture == $architecture)) | .digest // empty' \
[codex] +                "${target_dir}/registry-manifest.json")"
[codex] +            else
[codex] +              resolved_digest="$(jq -r '.digest // empty' "${target_dir}/registry-manifest.json")"
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +
[codex] +            manifest_digest="$(jq -r '.digest // empty' "${target_dir}/registry-manifest.json")"
[codex] +            if [[ -n "${declared_digest}" && "${declared_digest}" != "${manifest_digest}" ]]; then
[codex] +              jq -n \
[codex] +                --arg result declared-digest-mismatch \

[codex] +                --arg registry_digest "${manifest_digest}" \

[codex] +                > "${target_dir}/status.json"

[codex] +                "${platform}" "${source_ref}" "${source_pin}" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
[codex] +              incomplete=1
[codex] +              continue
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +
[codex] +            if [[ -z "${resolved_digest}" ]]; then
[codex] +              jq -n --arg result platform-manifest-not-found '{result: $result}' \
[codex] +                > "${target_dir}/status.json"

[codex] +                "${platform}" "${source_ref}" "${source_pin}" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
[codex] +              incomplete=1
[codex] +              continue
[codex] +            fi

[codex] +            repository="${source_ref%@*}"
[codex] +            last_component="${repository##*/}"
[codex] +            if [[ "${last_component}" == *:* ]]; then
[codex] +              repository="${repository%:*}"
[codex] +            fi

[codex] +

[codex] +              "${os_packages}" "${application_packages}" "${critical}" "${high}" "${result}" \

[codex] +#!/usr/bin/env bash
[codex] +# Render the repository-owned image inputs used by exact-image security scans.
[codex] +
[codex] +set -euo pipefail
[codex] +
[codex] +SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
[codex] +REPO_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
[codex] +
[codex] +# shellcheck source=deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh
[codex] +# shellcheck disable=SC1091 # The repository root is resolved above.
[codex] +. "${REPO_DIR}/deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh"
[codex] +
[codex] +OUTPUT_DIR=""
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM=""
[codex] +
[codex] +usage() {
[codex] +    cat &lt;&lt;'EOF'
[codex] +Usage: scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh --output-dir DIR [--local-platform PLATFORM]
[codex] +
[codex] +Renders the production Kustomize overlays and pinned controller charts without
[codex] +contacting a Kubernetes API. Helm values and observability post-renderers match
[codex] +the checked-in production install path. Local-only Kind and build-image sources
[codex] +are copied or extracted into a separate platform directory.
[codex] +
[codex] +PLATFORM uses the Trivy/Docker form linux/amd64 or linux/arm64. When omitted,
[codex] +the local platform is derived from uname.
[codex] +EOF
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +die() {
[codex] +    echo "ERROR: $*" >&2
[codex] +    exit 1
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +require_command() {
[codex] +    command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "required command not found: $1"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +default_local_platform() {
[codex] +    local architecture
[codex] +
[codex] +    case "$(uname -m)" in
[codex] +        x86_64|amd64)
[codex] +            architecture="amd64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        arm64|aarch64)
[codex] +            architecture="arm64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unsupported local architecture: $(uname -m)"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +
[codex] +    printf 'linux/%s\n' "${architecture}"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
[codex] +    case "$1" in
[codex] +        --output-dir)
[codex] +            OUTPUT_DIR="${2:-}"
[codex] +            shift 2
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        --local-platform)
[codex] +            LOCAL_PLATFORM="${2:-}"
[codex] +            shift 2
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        -h|--help)
[codex] +            usage
[codex] +            exit 0
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unknown argument: $1"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +done
[codex] +
[codex] +[[ -n "${OUTPUT_DIR}" ]] || die "--output-dir is required"
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM="${LOCAL_PLATFORM:-$(default_local_platform)}"
[codex] +case "${LOCAL_PLATFORM}" in
[codex] +    linux/amd64|linux/arm64)
[codex] +        ;;
[codex] +    *)
[codex] +        die "unsupported local platform: ${LOCAL_PLATFORM}"
[codex] +        ;;
[codex] +esac
[codex] +
[codex] +require_command helm
[codex] +require_command kubectl
[codex] +require_command install
[codex] +
[codex] +ARM64_DIR="${OUTPUT_DIR}/linux-arm64"
[codex] +LOCAL_DIR="${OUTPUT_DIR}/${LOCAL_PLATFORM//\//-}"
[codex] +mkdir -p "${ARM64_DIR}" "${LOCAL_DIR}"
[codex] +
[codex] +KUBE_VERSION="${PHASE4_K3S_VERSION#v}"
[codex] +KUBE_VERSION="${KUBE_VERSION%%+*}"
[codex] +
[codex] +helm template istio-base base \
[codex] +    --repo "${PHASE4_ISTIO_HELM_REPO_URL}" \
[codex] +    --namespace istio-system \
[codex] +    --version "${PHASE4_ISTIO_CHART_VERSION}" \
[codex] +    --kube-version "${KUBE_VERSION}" \
[codex] +    > "${ARM64_DIR}/istio-base.yaml"
[codex] +
[codex] +helm template istio-cni cni \
[codex] +    --repo "${PHASE4_ISTIO_HELM_REPO_URL}" \
[codex] +    --namespace istio-system \

[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +
[codex] +    printf 'linux/%s\n' "${architecture}"

[codex] +#!/usr/bin/env bash
[codex] +# Render the repository-owned image inputs used by exact-image security scans.
[codex] +
[codex] +set -euo pipefail
[codex] +
[codex] +SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
[codex] +REPO_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"

[codex] +# shellcheck source=deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh
[codex] +# shellcheck disable=SC1091 # The repository root is resolved above.
[codex] +. "${REPO_DIR}/deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh"
[codex] +
[codex] +OUTPUT_DIR=""
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM=""
[codex] +
[codex] +usage() {
[codex] +    cat &lt;&lt;'EOF'
[codex] +Usage: scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh --output-dir DIR [--local-platform PLATFORM]
[codex] +
[codex] +Renders the production Kustomize overlays and pinned controller charts without
[codex] +contacting a Kubernetes API. Helm values and observability post-renderers match
[codex] +the checked-in production install path. Local-only Kind and build-image sources
[codex] +are copied or extracted into a separate platform directory.
[codex] +
[codex] +PLATFORM uses the Trivy/Docker form linux/amd64 or linux/arm64. When omitted,
[codex] +the local platform is derived from uname.
[codex] +EOF
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +die() {
[codex] +    echo "ERROR: $*" >&2
[codex] +    exit 1
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +require_command() {
[codex] +    command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "required command not found: $1"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +default_local_platform() {
[codex] +    local architecture
[codex] +
[codex] +    case "$(uname -m)" in
[codex] +        x86_64|amd64)
[codex] +            architecture="amd64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        arm64|aarch64)
[codex] +            architecture="arm64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unsupported local architecture: $(uname -m)"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +
[codex] +    printf 'linux/%s\n' "${architecture}"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do

[codex] +        --local-platform)
[codex] +            LOCAL_PLATFORM="${2:-}"
[codex] +            shift 2
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        -h|--help)
[codex] +            usage
[codex] +            exit 0
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unknown argument: $1"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac

[codex] +[[ -n "${OUTPUT_DIR}" ]] || die "--output-dir is required"

[codex] +    linux/amd64|linux/arm64)
[codex] +        ;;
[codex] +    *)
[codex] +        die "unsupported local platform: ${LOCAL_PLATFORM}"
[codex] +        ;;

[codex] +          target_index=0
[codex] +          while IFS= read -r target; do
[codex] +            target_index=$((target_index + 1))
[codex] +            platform="$(jq -r '.platform' &lt;&lt;&lt; "${target}")"
[codex] +            source_ref="$(jq -r '.source_ref' &lt;&lt;&lt; "${target}")"
[codex] +            sources="$(jq -c '.sources' &lt;&lt;&lt; "${target}")"
[codex] +            target_hash="$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "${platform}" "${source_ref}" | sha256sum | cut -c1-12)"
[codex] +            target_dir="scan-work/evidence/$(printf '%03d' "${target_index}")-${target_hash}"
[codex] +            mkdir -p "${target_dir}"
[codex] +
[codex] +            if [[ "${source_ref}" == *@sha256:* ]]; then

[codex] +            else
[codex] +              source_pin="mutable"
[codex] +              declared_digest=""
[codex] +            fi

[codex] +              --arg source_ref "${source_ref}" \
[codex] +              --arg source_pin "${source_pin}" \

[codex] +              "{platform: \$platform, source_ref: \$source_ref, source_pin: \$source_pin, sources: \$sources}" \
[codex] +              > "${target_dir}/source.json"
[codex] +

[codex] +                --arg result offline-render-does-not-identify-image \

[codex] +              printf '| `%s` | `%s` | %s | - | - | - | - | - | offline render does not identify image |\n' \
[codex] +                "${platform}" "${source_ref}" "${source_pin}" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
[codex] +              incomplete=1
[codex] +              continue
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +
[codex] +            if ! docker buildx imagetools inspect --format '{{json .Manifest}}' "${source_ref}" \

[codex] +              2> "${target_dir}/registry-resolution.stderr"; then
[codex] +              jq -n --arg result registry-resolution-failed "{result: \$result}" \
[codex] +                > "${target_dir}/status.json"
[codex] +              # shellcheck disable=SC2016
[codex] +              printf '| `%s` | `%s` | %s | - | - | - | - | - | registry resolution failed |\n' \
[codex] +                "${platform}" "${source_ref}" "${source_pin}" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
[codex] +              incomplete=1
[codex] +              continue
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +
[codex] +            os="${platform%/*}"
[codex] +            architecture="${platform#*/}"
[codex] +            if jq -e '.manifests | type == "array"' "${target_dir}/registry-manifest.json" >/dev/null; then
[codex] +              resolved_digest="$(jq -r \
[codex] +                --arg os "${os}" \
[codex] +                --arg architecture "${architecture}" \
[codex] +                "first(.manifests[] | select(.platform.os == \$os and .platform.architecture == \$architecture)) | .digest // empty" \
[codex] +                "${target_dir}/registry-manifest.json")"
[codex] +            else
[codex] +              resolved_digest="$(jq -r '.digest // empty' "${target_dir}/registry-manifest.json")"
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +
[codex] +            manifest_digest="$(jq -r '.digest // empty' "${target_dir}/registry-manifest.json")"
[codex] +            if [[ -n "${declared_digest}" && "${declared_digest}" != "${manifest_digest}" ]]; then
[codex] +              jq -n \
[codex] +                --arg result declared-digest-mismatch \
[codex] +                --arg declared_digest "${declared_digest}" \
[codex] +                --arg registry_digest "${manifest_digest}" \
[codex] +                "{result: \$result, declared_digest: \$declared_digest, registry_digest: \$registry_digest}" \
[codex] +                > "${target_dir}/status.json"
[codex] +              # shellcheck disable=SC2016
[codex] +              printf '| `%s` | `%s` | %s | - | - | - | - | - | declared digest mismatch |\n' \
[codex] +                "${platform}" "${source_ref}" "${source_pin}" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
[codex] +              incomplete=1
[codex] +              continue
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +
[codex] +            if [[ -z "${resolved_digest}" ]]; then
[codex] +              jq -n --arg result platform-manifest-not-found "{result: \$result}" \
[codex] +                > "${target_dir}/status.json"
[codex] +              # shellcheck disable=SC2016
[codex] +              printf '| `%s` | `%s` | %s | - | - | - | - | - | platform manifest not found |\n' \
[codex] +                "${platform}" "${source_ref}" "${source_pin}" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
[codex] +              incomplete=1
[codex] +              continue
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +
[codex] +            repository="${source_ref%@*}"
[codex] +            last_component="${repository##*/}"
[codex] +            if [[ "${last_component}" == *:* ]]; then
[codex] +              repository="${repository%:*}"
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +            resolved_ref="${repository}@${resolved_digest}"
[codex] +
[codex] +            jq -n \
[codex] +              --arg platform "${platform}" \
[codex] +              --arg source_ref "${source_ref}" \

[codex] +                source_ref: \$source_ref,
[codex] +                source_pin: \$source_pin,
[codex] +                source_manifest_digest: \$source_manifest_digest,
[codex] +                resolved_ref: \$resolved_ref,
[codex] +                resolved_digest: \$resolved_digest,
[codex] +                sources: \$sources
[codex] +              }" > "${target_dir}/resolved-artifact.json"
[codex] +
[codex] +            inventory_ok=true

[codex] +              incomplete=1
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +

[codex] +              --platform "${platform}" \
[codex] +              --scanners vuln \

[codex] +              "${resolved_ref}" \
[codex] +              2> "${target_dir}/vulnerabilities.stderr"; then
[codex] +              vulnerabilities_ok=false
[codex] +              incomplete=1
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +

[codex] +                "{result: \$result, inventory_complete: \$inventory_ok, vulnerability_report_complete: \$vulnerabilities_ok}" \
[codex] +                > "${target_dir}/status.json"
[codex] +              # shellcheck disable=SC2016
[codex] +              printf '| `%s` | `%s` | %s | - | - | - | - | - | Trivy scan failed |\n' \

[codex] +              continue
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +
[codex] +            os_id="$(jq -r '(.Metadata.OS.Family // "unidentified") + ":" + (.Metadata.OS.Name // "unidentified")' \

[codex] +            else

[codex] +            fi

[codex] +              "{
[codex] +                result: \$result,
[codex] +                os: \$os,
[codex] +                os_packages: \$os_packages,
[codex] +                application_packages: \$application_packages,

[codex] +#!/usr/bin/env bash
[codex] +# Render the repository-owned image inputs used by exact-image security scans.
[codex] +
[codex] +set -euo pipefail
[codex] +
[codex] +SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
[codex] +REPO_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
[codex] +
[codex] +# shellcheck source=deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh
[codex] +# shellcheck disable=SC1091 # The repository root is resolved above.
[codex] +. "${REPO_DIR}/deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh"
[codex] +
[codex] +OUTPUT_DIR=""
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM=""
[codex] +
[codex] +usage() {
[codex] +    cat &lt;&lt;'EOF'
[codex] +Usage: scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh --output-dir DIR [--local-platform PLATFORM]
[codex] +
[codex] +Renders the production Kustomize overlays and pinned controller charts without
[codex] +contacting a Kubernetes API. Helm values and observability post-renderers match
[codex] +the checked-in production install path. Local-only Kind and build-image sources
[codex] +are copied or extracted into a separate platform directory.
[codex] +
[codex] +PLATFORM uses the Trivy/Docker form linux/amd64 or linux/arm64. When omitted,
[codex] +the local platform is derived from uname.
[codex] +EOF
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +die() {
[codex] +    echo "ERROR: $*" >&2
[codex] +    exit 1
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +require_command() {
[codex] +    command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "required command not found: $1"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +default_local_platform() {
[codex] +    local architecture
[codex] +
[codex] +    case "$(uname -m)" in
[codex] +        x86_64|amd64)
[codex] +            architecture="amd64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        arm64|aarch64)
[codex] +            architecture="arm64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unsupported local architecture: $(uname -m)"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +
[codex] +    printf 'linux/%s\n' "${architecture}"
[codex] +}

[codex] +          {

[codex] +          target_index=0

[codex] +                "${platform}" "${source_ref}" "${source_pin}" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
[codex] +              incomplete=1
[codex] +              continue
[codex] +            fi

[codex] +              incomplete=1
[codex] +              continue
[codex] +            fi

[codex] +#!/usr/bin/env bash
[codex] +# Render the repository-owned image inputs used by exact-image security scans.
[codex] +
[codex] +set -euo pipefail
[codex] +
[codex] +SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
[codex] +REPO_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
[codex] +
[codex] +# shellcheck source=deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh
[codex] +# shellcheck disable=SC1091 # The repository root is resolved above.
[codex] +. "${REPO_DIR}/deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh"
[codex] +
[codex] +OUTPUT_DIR=""
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM=""
[codex] +
[codex] +usage() {
[codex] +    cat &lt;&lt;'EOF'
[codex] +Usage: scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh --output-dir DIR [--local-platform PLATFORM]
[codex] +
[codex] +Renders the production Kustomize overlays and pinned controller charts without
[codex] +contacting a Kubernetes API. Helm values and observability post-renderers match
[codex] +the checked-in production install path. Local-only Kind and build-image sources
[codex] +are copied or extracted into a separate platform directory.
[codex] +
[codex] +PLATFORM uses the Trivy/Docker form linux/amd64 or linux/arm64. When omitted,
[codex] +the local platform is derived from uname.
[codex] +EOF
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +die() {
[codex] +    echo "ERROR: $*" >&2
[codex] +    exit 1
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +require_command() {
[codex] +    command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "required command not found: $1"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +default_local_platform() {
[codex] +    local architecture
[codex] +
[codex] +    case "$(uname -m)" in
[codex] +        x86_64|amd64)
[codex] +            architecture="amd64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        arm64|aarch64)
[codex] +            architecture="arm64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unsupported local architecture: $(uname -m)"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +
[codex] +    printf 'linux/%s\n' "${architecture}"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
[codex] +    case "$1" in
[codex] +        --output-dir)
[codex] +            OUTPUT_DIR="${2:-}"
[codex] +            shift 2
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        --local-platform)
[codex] +            LOCAL_PLATFORM="${2:-}"
[codex] +            shift 2
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        -h|--help)
[codex] +            usage
[codex] +            exit 0
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unknown argument: $1"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +done
[codex] +
[codex] +[[ -n "${OUTPUT_DIR}" ]] || die "--output-dir is required"
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM="${LOCAL_PLATFORM:-$(default_local_platform)}"
[codex] +case "${LOCAL_PLATFORM}" in
[codex] +    linux/amd64|linux/arm64)
[codex] +        ;;
[codex] +    *)
[codex] +        die "unsupported local platform: ${LOCAL_PLATFORM}"
[codex] +        ;;
[codex] +esac
[codex] +
[codex] +require_command helm
[codex] +require_command kubectl
[codex] +require_command install
[codex] +
[codex] +ARM64_DIR="${OUTPUT_DIR}/linux-arm64"
[codex] +LOCAL_DIR="${OUTPUT_DIR}/${LOCAL_PLATFORM//\//-}"

[codex] +              inventory_ok=false
[codex] +              incomplete=1
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +
[codex] +            vulnerabilities_ok=true
[codex] +            if ! trivy image \
[codex] +              --image-src remote \
[codex] +              --platform "${platform}" \
[codex] +              --scanners vuln \
[codex] +              --format json \

[codex] +              # shellcheck disable=SC2016

[codex] +                "${platform}" "${resolved_ref}" "${source_pin}" >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}"
[codex] +              continue
[codex] +            fi
[codex] +
[codex] +            os_id="$(jq -r '(.Metadata.OS.Family // "unidentified") + ":" + (.Metadata.OS.Name // "unidentified")' \

[codex] +              "${target_dir}/package-inventory.json")"

[codex] +            else
[codex] +              result="complete"
[codex] +            fi

[codex] +                result: \$result,
[codex] +                os: \$os,
[codex] +                os_packages: \$os_packages,
[codex] +                application_packages: \$application_packages,
[codex] +                vulnerabilities: {critical: \$critical, high: \$high}
[codex] +              }" > "${target_dir}/status.json"
[codex] +
[codex] +            # shellcheck disable=SC2016
[codex] +            printf '| `%s` | `%s` | %s | `%s` | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s |\n' \
[codex] +              "${platform}" "${resolved_ref}" "${source_pin}" "${os_id}" \
[codex] +              "${os_packages}" "${application_packages}" "${critical}" "${high}" "${result}" \

[codex] +        with:
[codex] +          cmd: |
[codex] +            set -eu
[codex] +            : > scan-work/raw-targets.tsv
[codex] +            for platform_dir in scan-work/rendered/linux-*; do
[codex] +              platform="linux/${platform_dir##*-}"
[codex] +              for manifest in "${platform_dir}"/*.yaml; do
[codex] +                source_path="${manifest#scan-work/rendered/}"
[codex] +                yq eval-all --no-doc --unwrapScalar '
[codex] +                  (
[codex] +                    .. | select(tag == "!!map") | .image? |
[codex] +                    select(tag == "!!str")
[codex] +                  ),
[codex] +                  (
[codex] +                    .. | select(tag == "!!seq") | .[] |
[codex] +                    select(

[codex] +                      test("^--(prometheus-config-reloader|acme-http01-solver-image)=")
[codex] +                    ) |
[codex] +                    sub("^--[^=]+="; "")
[codex] +                  )
[codex] +                ' "${manifest}" |
[codex] +                  while IFS= read -r image_ref; do
[codex] +                    case "${image_ref}" in
[codex] +                      ghcr.io/budgetanalyzer/*) continue ;;
[codex] +                    esac
[codex] +                    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "${source_path}" "${platform}" "${image_ref}" \
[codex] +                      >> scan-work/raw-targets.tsv
[codex] +                  done
[codex] +              done
[codex] +            done
[codex] +            sort -u scan-work/raw-targets.tsv -o scan-work/raw-targets.tsv
[codex] +
[codex] +      - name: Build the deduplicated scan target manifest
[codex] +        run: |
[codex] +          test -s scan-work/raw-targets.tsv
[codex] +          jq -Rn '
[codex] +            [
[codex] +              inputs |

[codex] +            ] |

[codex] +              platform: .[0].platform,
[codex] +              source_ref: .[0].source_ref,
[codex] +              sources: (map(.source) | unique)
[codex] +            })
[codex] +          ' &lt; scan-work/raw-targets.tsv > scan-work/targets.json

[codex]   warnings and migrations as failures; correct the preset or repository config.
[codex] - **No extraction:** check the owning file's native manager pattern or adjacent
[codex]   annotation and compare debug logs. Do not seed the historical expected version
[codex]   into configuration.
[codex] - **No lookup or wrong package:** verify the real datasource identity, chart
[codex]   name, registry URL, tag prefix, build suffix, and flavor suffix. Record an
[codex]   unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.
[codex] - **Authentication or resolution failure:** preserve the failure. Fix encrypted
[codex]   Maven/registry access in the supported trust boundary; do not use Maven Local,
[codex]   drop internal dependencies, or swallow the error.
[codex] - **Finding without an update:** retain the Dependabot/scanner finding and route
[codex]   inherited or transitive remediation to the owning service. An update pull
[codex]   request is not proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] - **CI failure on a bot branch:** determine whether the proposal needs its
[codex]   documented checksum, chart rendering, ARM64, state migration, or cross-repo
[codex]   companion review. Do not relax a guardrail or create orchestration drift.
[codex] - **Scanner database/download failure:** report the job as failed separately
[codex]   from vulnerability findings. Never turn an unavailable scan into a clean result.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate discovery and vulnerability scanners do not comprehensively establish
[codex] end-of-life status. Owners must still perform a quarterly support-policy review
[codex] against upstream lifecycle sources.
[codex] 
[codex] `service-common` is a library release line, not the stack version. Release it
[codex] when `spring-platform`, `spring-cloud-platform`, `service-core`, or
[codex] `service-web` changes. Do not bump it only to ship a service image, route
[codex] change, documentation metadata fix, or production overlay update.
[codex] 
[codex] Tag helpers remain useful for human source management and rare named releases,
[codex] but tag names are not production correctness. OCI apply and verification use
[codex] the checked-in desired state and immutable image digests.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Orchestration Workflows
[codex] 
[codex] Dependency update pull-request ownership, activation, cost constraints, and
[codex] failure triage live in [Dependency Automation](dependency-automation.md). The
[codex] focused `dependency-automation-config.yml` workflow runs Renovate's official
[codex] strict configuration validator against the repository config and shared preset;
[codex] it does not install the App or open dependency pull requests.
[codex] 
[codex] ### `security-guardrails.yml`
[codex] 
[codex] The orchestration repo now has a dedicated static security workflow for the
[codex] manifest guardrail suite. It is intentionally additive beside `test-setup.yml`;
[codex] it does not reuse the stale DinD suites as current security guardrails.
[codex] 
[codex] It now runs on every push to `main` and every pull request targeting `main`.
[codex] The narrower path filter was removed so guarded security surfaces cannot bypass
[codex] the workflow when a new file path is added to the static scope.
[codex] 
[codex] What it runs:
[codex] 
[codex] - `./scripts/guardrails/verify-static-security-manifests.sh`
[codex] - `./scripts/guardrails/verify-static-security-manifests.sh --self-test`
[codex] 
[codex] The workflow bootstraps repo-pinned `helm`, `kubectl`, `kubeconform`,
[codex] `kube-linter`, and `kyverno` binaries through
[codex] `scripts/bootstrap/install-verified-tool.sh`, then runs:
[codex] 
[codex] - schema validation for checked-in manifests, with explicit missing-schema
[codex]   allowances for checked-in CRD resources such as Istio, Gateway API, Kyverno,
[codex]   and Prometheus Operator `ServiceMonitor` objects
[codex] - rendered Kustomize schema validation for the production app and
[codex]   infrastructure overlays, so partial patch files stay excluded from
[codex]   standalone validation but are still checked after render; the schema-v2
[codex]   production deployment manifest is also excluded because it is desired-state
[codex]   metadata, not a Kubernetes resource
[codex] - repo-specific kube-linter checks with documented exceptions
[codex] - Kyverno CLI pass/fail fixtures
[codex] - a generated Kyverno replay for representative approved local Tilt
[codex]   `:tilt-&lt;hash>` deploy refs derived from the checked-in contract inventory
[codex] - a rendered Kyverno production-chart check that rejects mutable controller and
[codex]   hook image refs from `deploy/helm-values/kyverno.values.yaml`
[codex] - pattern scans for image pinning, namespace PSA labels, and lingering
[codex]   pipe-to-shell guidance in active setup docs/scripts
[codex] 
[codex] That directory split is intentional: CI-safe checks live under
[codex] `scripts/guardrails/`, shared installer/bootstrap helpers live under
[codex] `scripts/bootstrap/`, and the live-cluster proof remains in
[codex] `scripts/smoketest/` so GitHub Actions cannot silently drift into a
[codex] static-only substitute for the local runtime gate.
[codex] 
[codex] Use the same command locally to reproduce workflow failures without a cluster:
[codex] 
[codex] ```bash
[codex] ./scripts/guardrails/verify-static-security-manifests.sh
[codex] ```

[codex] ## Pilot evidence
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate `44.65.5` was initially run under Node `24.13.0` and rerun under the
[codex] workspace baseline Node `24.20.0` against a plain copy of the checkout. The
[codex] unpublished shared preset and repository configuration were merged in memory,
[codex] repository config discovery was suppressed, and local platform dry-run mode
[codex] was used with debug logging. This avoids resolving the not-yet-published GitHub
[codex] preset and includes newly created, untracked files.
[codex] 
[codex] The final extraction rerun found 98 occurrences in 34 package files:
[codex] 
[codex] | Manager | Files | Occurrences | Evidence |
[codex] | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
[codex] | Dockerfile | 1 | 1 | `nginx/Dockerfile.prod-smoke-assets` -> `alpine` |
[codex] | GitHub Actions | 3 | 11 | Both existing workflows plus the new validator workflow; checkout, setup-node, Node input, and runner identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Helm values | 2 | 13 | Kyverno digest overrides and five kube-prometheus-stack image identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Kubernetes | 11 | 29 | Stateful infrastructure, Jaeger, service init images, gateway images, local first-party images, and Kubernetes API kinds were recognized. |
[codex] | Regex | 17 | 44 | Shell/Tilt chart pins, tool releases, Kind, Kiali, inline Temurin, probe images, Playwright, and the Renovate validator were recognized. |
[codex] 
[codex] Three of the GitHub Actions occurrences come from the manual hosted-dry-run job
[codex] and repeat already-covered runner, setup-node, and Node identities; they do not
[codex] add a new dependency surface.
[codex] 
[codex] The first lookup run completed in about 34 seconds and reported 57 distinct
[codex] dependency records, 31 outdated records, and 104 candidate branches before
[codex] routine limits and dashboard approvals. Live lookups succeeded for all six
[codex] configured Helm repositories, npm, and most container registries. The final
[codex] rerun completed lookup and returned 101 candidate branches, with the expected
[codex] missing-GitHub-token warning and an anonymous Docker token warning. Registry
[codex] lookup failures are retained below instead of being presented as a clean scan.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate's documented local platform supports `extract` and `lookup`, not a
[codex] true `full` dry run. Passing `--dry-run=full` falls back to lookup behavior.
[codex] Therefore extraction and live lookup are demonstrated locally, but branch-file
[codex] mutation and the published preset resolution still require a no-write hosted
[codex] observation after publication. No GitHub token was available in this worker,
[codex] by design, so GitHub-backed identities were extracted with
[codex] `github-token-required` and were not looked up. Those lookups are deferred to
[codex] the user-triggered Phase 12 job, which receives its ephemeral read-only token
[codex] inside GitHub Actions.

[codex] +#!/usr/bin/env bash
[codex] +# Render the repository-owned image inputs used by exact-image security scans.
[codex] +
[codex] +set -euo pipefail
[codex] +
[codex] +SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
[codex] +REPO_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
[codex] +
[codex] +# shellcheck source=deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh
[codex] +# shellcheck disable=SC1091 # The repository root is resolved above.
[codex] +. "${REPO_DIR}/deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh"
[codex] +
[codex] +OUTPUT_DIR=""
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM=""
[codex] +
[codex] +usage() {
[codex] +    cat &lt;&lt;'EOF'
[codex] +Usage: scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh --output-dir DIR [--local-platform PLATFORM]
[codex] +
[codex] +Renders the production Kustomize overlays and pinned controller charts without
[codex] +contacting a Kubernetes API. Helm values and observability post-renderers match
[codex] +the checked-in production install path. Local-only Kind and build-image sources
[codex] +are copied or extracted into a separate platform directory.
[codex] +
[codex] +PLATFORM uses the Trivy/Docker form linux/amd64 or linux/arm64. When omitted,
[codex] +the local platform is derived from uname.
[codex] +EOF
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +die() {
[codex] +    echo "ERROR: $*" >&2
[codex] +    exit 1
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +require_command() {
[codex] +    command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "required command not found: $1"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +default_local_platform() {
[codex] +    local architecture
[codex] +
[codex] +    case "$(uname -m)" in
[codex] +        x86_64|amd64)
[codex] +            architecture="amd64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        arm64|aarch64)
[codex] +            architecture="arm64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unsupported local architecture: $(uname -m)"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +
[codex] +    printf 'linux/%s\n' "${architecture}"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
[codex] +    case "$1" in
[codex] +        --output-dir)
[codex] +            OUTPUT_DIR="${2:-}"
[codex] +            shift 2
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        --local-platform)
[codex] +            LOCAL_PLATFORM="${2:-}"
[codex] +            shift 2
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        -h|--help)
[codex] +            usage
[codex] +            exit 0
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unknown argument: $1"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +done
[codex] +
[codex] +[[ -n "${OUTPUT_DIR}" ]] || die "--output-dir is required"
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM="${LOCAL_PLATFORM:-$(default_local_platform)}"
[codex] +case "${LOCAL_PLATFORM}" in
[codex] +    linux/amd64|linux/arm64)
[codex] +        ;;
[codex] +    *)
[codex] +        die "unsupported local platform: ${LOCAL_PLATFORM}"
[codex] +        ;;
[codex] +esac
[codex] +
[codex] +require_command helm
[codex] +require_command kubectl
[codex] +require_command install
[codex] +
[codex] +ARM64_DIR="${OUTPUT_DIR}/linux-arm64"
[codex] +LOCAL_DIR="${OUTPUT_DIR}/${LOCAL_PLATFORM//\//-}"
[codex] +mkdir -p "${ARM64_DIR}" "${LOCAL_DIR}"
[codex] +
[codex] +KUBE_VERSION="${PHASE4_K3S_VERSION#v}"
[codex] +KUBE_VERSION="${KUBE_VERSION%%+*}"
[codex] +
[codex] +helm template istio-base base \
[codex] +    --repo "${PHASE4_ISTIO_HELM_REPO_URL}" \
[codex] +    --namespace istio-system \
[codex] +    --version "${PHASE4_ISTIO_CHART_VERSION}" \
[codex] +    --kube-version "${KUBE_VERSION}" \
[codex] +    > "${ARM64_DIR}/istio-base.yaml"
[codex] +
[codex] +helm template istio-cni cni \
[codex] +    --repo "${PHASE4_ISTIO_HELM_REPO_URL}" \
[codex] +    --namespace istio-system \
[codex] +    --version "${PHASE4_ISTIO_CHART_VERSION}" \
[codex] +    --values "${REPO_DIR}/kubernetes/istio/cni-common-values.yaml" \

[codex] +#!/usr/bin/env bash
[codex] +# Render the repository-owned image inputs used by exact-image security scans.
[codex] +
[codex] +set -euo pipefail
[codex] +

[codex] +# shellcheck disable=SC1091 # The repository root is resolved above.

[codex] +
[codex] +OUTPUT_DIR=""
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM=""

[codex] +usage() {
[codex] +    cat &lt;&lt;'EOF'
[codex] +Usage: scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh --output-dir DIR [--local-platform PLATFORM]
[codex] +
[codex] +Renders the production Kustomize overlays and pinned controller charts without
[codex] +contacting a Kubernetes API. Helm values and observability post-renderers match
[codex] +the checked-in production install path. Local-only Kind and build-image sources
[codex] +are copied or extracted into a separate platform directory.

[codex] +PLATFORM uses the Trivy/Docker form linux/amd64 or linux/arm64. When omitted,

[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +
[codex] +    printf 'linux/%s\n' "${architecture}"
[codex] +}
