[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as unscannable and fails as incomplete rather than adding a live-cluster
[codex] +dependency or claiming a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +

[codex] +#!/usr/bin/env bash
[codex] +# Render the repository-owned image inputs used by exact-image security scans.
[codex] +
[codex] +set -euo pipefail
[codex] +
[codex] +SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
[codex] +REPO_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
[codex] +

[codex] +contacting a Kubernetes API. Helm values and observability post-renderers match
[codex] +the checked-in production install path. Local-only Kind and build-image sources
[codex] +are copied or extracted into a separate platform directory.

[codex] +default_local_platform() {

[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as unscannable and fails as incomplete rather than adding a live-cluster
[codex] +dependency or claiming a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as unscannable and fails as incomplete rather than adding a live-cluster
[codex] +dependency or claiming a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +
[codex]  ## Failure triage

[codex] +        uses: mikefarah/yq@e1d5d6eb36b8995bf29e5acb561659824dc47be3 # v4.53.6
[codex] +        with:
[codex] +          cmd: |
[codex] +            set -eu
[codex] +            : > scan-work/raw-targets.tsv
[codex] +            for platform_dir in scan-work/rendered/linux-*; do
[codex] +              platform="linux/${platform_dir##*-}"
[codex] +              for manifest in "${platform_dir}"/*.yaml; do
[codex] +                source_path="${manifest#scan-work/rendered/}"
[codex] +                yq eval-all --no-doc --unwrapScalar '
[codex] +                  (
[codex] +                    .. | select(tag == "!!map") | .image? |
[codex] +                    select(tag == "!!str")
[codex] +                  ),
[codex] +                  (
[codex] +                    .. | select(tag == "!!seq") | .[] |
[codex] +                    select(
[codex] +                      tag == "!!str" and
[codex] +                      test("^--(prometheus-config-reloader|acme-http01-solver-image)=")
[codex] +                    ) |
[codex] +                    sub("^--[^=]+="; "")
[codex] +                  )
[codex] +                ' "${manifest}" |
[codex] +                  while IFS= read -r image_ref; do
[codex] +                    case "${image_ref}" in
[codex] +                      ghcr.io/budgetanalyzer/*) continue ;;
[codex] +                    esac
[codex] +                    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "${source_path}" "${platform}" "${image_ref}" \
[codex] +                      >> scan-work/raw-targets.tsv
[codex] +                  done
[codex] +              done
[codex] +            done
[codex] +            sort -u scan-work/raw-targets.tsv -o scan-work/raw-targets.tsv
[codex] +
[codex] +      - name: Build the deduplicated scan target manifest
[codex] +        run: |
[codex] +          test -s scan-work/raw-targets.tsv
[codex] +          jq -Rn '
[codex] +            [
[codex] +              inputs |
[codex] +              split("\t") |
[codex] +              {source: .[0], platform: .[1], source_ref: .[2]}
[codex] +            ] |
[codex] +            group_by([.platform, .source_ref]) |
[codex] +            map({
[codex] +              platform: .[0].platform,

[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as unscannable and fails as incomplete rather than adding a live-cluster
[codex] +dependency or claiming a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as unscannable and fails as incomplete rather than adding a live-cluster
[codex] +dependency or claiming a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as unscannable and fails as incomplete rather than adding a live-cluster
[codex] +dependency or claiming a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +

[codex] +#!/usr/bin/env bash
[codex] +# Render the repository-owned image inputs used by exact-image security scans.
[codex] +
[codex] +set -euo pipefail
[codex] +
[codex] +SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
[codex] +REPO_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
[codex] +
[codex] +# shellcheck source=deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh
[codex] +# shellcheck disable=SC1091 # The repository root is resolved above.
[codex] +. "${REPO_DIR}/deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh"
[codex] +
[codex] +OUTPUT_DIR=""
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM=""
[codex] +
[codex] +usage() {
[codex] +    cat &lt;&lt;'EOF'
[codex] +Usage: scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh --output-dir DIR [--local-platform PLATFORM]
[codex] +
[codex] +Renders the production Kustomize overlays and pinned controller charts without
[codex] +contacting a Kubernetes API. Helm values and observability post-renderers match
[codex] +the checked-in production install path. Local-only Kind and build-image sources
[codex] +are copied or extracted into a separate platform directory.
[codex] +
[codex] +PLATFORM uses the Trivy/Docker form linux/amd64 or linux/arm64. When omitted,
[codex] +the local platform is derived from uname.
[codex] +EOF
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +die() {
[codex] +    echo "ERROR: $*" >&2
[codex] +    exit 1
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +require_command() {
[codex] +    command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "required command not found: $1"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +default_local_platform() {
[codex] +    local architecture

[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as unscannable and fails as incomplete rather than adding a live-cluster
[codex] +dependency or claiming a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +

[codex] +#!/usr/bin/env bash
[codex] +# Render the repository-owned image inputs used by exact-image security scans.
[codex] +
[codex] +set -euo pipefail
[codex] +
[codex] +SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
[codex] +REPO_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
[codex] +
[codex] +# shellcheck source=deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh
[codex] +# shellcheck disable=SC1091 # The repository root is resolved above.
[codex] +. "${REPO_DIR}/deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh"
[codex] +
[codex] +OUTPUT_DIR=""
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM=""
[codex] +
[codex] +usage() {
[codex] +    cat &lt;&lt;'EOF'
[codex] +Usage: scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh --output-dir DIR [--local-platform PLATFORM]
[codex] +
[codex] +Renders the production Kustomize overlays and pinned controller charts without
[codex] +contacting a Kubernetes API. Helm values and observability post-renderers match
[codex] +the checked-in production install path. Local-only Kind and build-image sources
[codex] +are copied or extracted into a separate platform directory.
[codex] +
[codex] +PLATFORM uses the Trivy/Docker form linux/amd64 or linux/arm64. When omitted,
[codex] +the local platform is derived from uname.
[codex] +EOF
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +die() {
[codex] +    echo "ERROR: $*" >&2
[codex] +    exit 1
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +require_command() {
[codex] +    command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "required command not found: $1"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +default_local_platform() {
[codex] +    local architecture
[codex] +
[codex] +    case "$(uname -m)" in
[codex] +        x86_64|amd64)
[codex] +            architecture="amd64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        arm64|aarch64)
[codex] +            architecture="arm64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unsupported local architecture: $(uname -m)"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +
[codex] +    printf 'linux/%s\n' "${architecture}"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
[codex] +    case "$1" in
[codex] +        --output-dir)
[codex] +            OUTPUT_DIR="${2:-}"
[codex] +            shift 2
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        --local-platform)
[codex] +            LOCAL_PLATFORM="${2:-}"
[codex] +            shift 2
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        -h|--help)
[codex] +            usage
[codex] +            exit 0
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unknown argument: $1"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac

[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as unscannable and fails as incomplete rather than adding a live-cluster
[codex] +dependency or claiming a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +

[codex] +#!/usr/bin/env bash
[codex] +# Render the repository-owned image inputs used by exact-image security scans.
[codex] +
[codex] +set -euo pipefail
[codex] +
[codex] +SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
[codex] +REPO_DIR="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
[codex] +
[codex] +# shellcheck source=deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh
[codex] +# shellcheck disable=SC1091 # The repository root is resolved above.
[codex] +. "${REPO_DIR}/deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh"
[codex] +
[codex] +OUTPUT_DIR=""
[codex] +LOCAL_PLATFORM=""
[codex] +
[codex] +usage() {
[codex] +    cat &lt;&lt;'EOF'
[codex] +Usage: scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh --output-dir DIR [--local-platform PLATFORM]
[codex] +
[codex] +Renders the production Kustomize overlays and pinned controller charts without
[codex] +contacting a Kubernetes API. Helm values and observability post-renderers match
[codex] +the checked-in production install path. Local-only Kind and build-image sources
[codex] +are copied or extracted into a separate platform directory.
[codex] +
[codex] +PLATFORM uses the Trivy/Docker form linux/amd64 or linux/arm64. When omitted,
[codex] +the local platform is derived from uname.
[codex] +EOF
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +die() {
[codex] +    echo "ERROR: $*" >&2
[codex] +    exit 1
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +require_command() {
[codex] +    command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "required command not found: $1"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +default_local_platform() {
[codex] +    local architecture
[codex] +
[codex] +    case "$(uname -m)" in
[codex] +        x86_64|amd64)
[codex] +            architecture="amd64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        arm64|aarch64)
[codex] +            architecture="arm64"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unsupported local architecture: $(uname -m)"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +
[codex] +    printf 'linux/%s\n' "${architecture}"
[codex] +}
[codex] +
[codex] +while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
[codex] +    case "$1" in
[codex] +        --output-dir)
[codex] +            OUTPUT_DIR="${2:-}"
[codex] +            shift 2
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        --local-platform)
[codex] +            LOCAL_PLATFORM="${2:-}"
[codex] +            shift 2
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        -h|--help)
[codex] +            usage
[codex] +            exit 0
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +        *)
[codex] +            die "unknown argument: $1"
[codex] +            ;;
[codex] +    esac
[codex] +done
[codex] +

[codex] +    linux/amd64|linux/arm64)
[codex] +        ;;
[codex] +    *)
[codex] +        die "unsupported local platform: ${LOCAL_PLATFORM}"

[codex] +KUBE_VERSION="${KUBE_VERSION%%+*}"
[codex] +

[codex] +    --repo "${PHASE4_ISTIO_HELM_REPO_URL}" \

[codex] +    --kube-version "${KUBE_VERSION}" \

[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as unscannable and fails as incomplete rather than adding a live-cluster
[codex] +dependency or claiming a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as unscannable and fails as incomplete rather than adding a live-cluster
[codex] +dependency or claiming a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as unscannable and fails as incomplete rather than adding a live-cluster
[codex] +dependency or claiming a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as unscannable and fails as incomplete rather than adding a live-cluster
[codex] +dependency or claiming a clean result.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as a known unscannable gap rather than adding a live-cluster dependency
[codex] +or claiming coverage. Unexpected render, resolution, database, or scan failures
[codex] +still fail the job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +

[codex] +## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] +
[codex] +`exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] +no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] +when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] +vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] +scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] +for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] +
[codex] +The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] +the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] +`deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] +Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] +operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] +standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] +frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] +release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] +Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] +hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] +
[codex] +- the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] +- the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] +- a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] +- a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] +- Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex] +  machine-readable completion status
[codex] +
[codex] +A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] +immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] +difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] +desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] +`ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] +value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] +digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] +
[codex] +The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] +`guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] +they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] +scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] +post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] +known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] +only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] +target as a known unscannable gap rather than adding a live-cluster dependency
[codex] +or claiming coverage. Unexpected render, resolution, database, or scan failures
[codex] +still fail the job.
[codex] +
[codex] +Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] +an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] +known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] +Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] +package scan.
[codex] +

[codex] ## Local validation and dry run
[codex] 
[codex] The focused workflow validates both JSON files with Renovate's official
[codex] `renovate-config-validator` under Node 24. Before publishing the preset, run the
[codex] same strict schema validation locally. For an unpublished-preset dry run, load
[codex] `renovate-presets/default.json` as the local self-hosted configuration, suppress
[codex] repository config discovery, and process the checkout with the local platform.
[codex] Use debug logging and do not provide a GitHub token or enable a write-capable
[codex] platform mode. Local mode proves extraction and supported lookups but does not
[codex] perform a true full dry run. Phase 12 owns the post-publication GitHub-platform
[codex] full dry run through the manually dispatched, read-only workflow; its ephemeral
[codex] job token is never provided to an agent.
[codex] 
[codex] Extraction and lookup evidence belongs in
[codex] [`docs/research/dependency-automation-coverage.md`](research/dependency-automation-coverage.md),
[codex] not in a second desired-version inventory.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Exact-image security evidence
[codex] 
[codex] `exact-image-security-evidence.yml` runs weekly and by manual dispatch. It has
[codex] no pull-request trigger and findings do not create a merge gate. The job fails
[codex] when rendering, registry resolution, database download, package inventory, or a
[codex] vulnerability scan is incomplete; vulnerability findings themselves leave the
[codex] scan successful. The final upload runs even after failure and retains evidence
[codex] for seven days without relying on SARIF hosting or a paid service.
[codex] 
[codex] The workflow calls `scripts/security/render-image-scan-inputs.sh`, which uses
[codex] the production Kustomize overlays, controller chart versions from
[codex] `deploy/scripts/lib/version-contract.sh`, their checked-in values, and the
[codex] Prometheus/Kiali post-renderers. It includes Helm-created controllers and hooks,
[codex] operator-supplied cert-manager solver and Prometheus config-reloader images,
[codex] standalone Jaeger and infrastructure images, and the Tilt Temurin, Kind, and
[codex] frontend production-smoke images. First-party service images remain under the
[codex] release workflow and are excluded from this scanner job.
[codex] 
[codex] Production/controller images are resolved and scanned as `linux/arm64`.
[codex] Local-only sources use the actual scanner-runner platform (`linux/amd64` on the
[codex] hosted job). For each deduplicated target, the artifact contains:
[codex] 
[codex] - the rendered source ref and every file that contributed it
[codex] - the registry manifest and the selected platform child digest
[codex] - a Trivy all-package JSON inventory with OS and application package classes
[codex] - a separate JSON vulnerability report plus captured stderr
[codex] - Trivy CLI and vulnerability-database metadata, database-download logs, and a
[codex]   machine-readable completion status
[codex] 
[codex] A rendered tag without a digest is labelled `mutable` even though the job
[codex] immediately resolves and scans one exact platform digest. This preserves the
[codex] difference between repeatable evidence for that run and immutable checked-in
[codex] desired state. In particular, External Secrets chart 2.2.0 currently renders
[codex] `ghcr.io/external-secrets/external-secrets:v2.2.0`; its checked-in `image.digest`
[codex] value is not emitted by that chart version. The tag resolved to the intended
[codex] digest during Phase 2 validation, but later tag movement remains possible.
[codex] 
[codex] The existing `deploy/scripts/render/observability.sh` and
[codex] `guardrails/verify-production-image-overlay.sh` are not CI render entry points:
[codex] they intentionally use a live server-side Helm dry run for Kiali RBAC. The
[codex] scanner invokes ordinary `helm template` with the same Kiali values and
[codex] post-renderer, so it needs no Kubernetes API or production credentials. One
[codex] known gap remains explicit: the Istio gateway chart renders `image: auto`, and
[codex] only a live Istio injector chooses the proxy image. The workflow records that
[codex] target as a known unscannable gap rather than adding a live-cluster dependency
[codex] or claiming coverage. Unexpected render, resolution, database, or scan failures
[codex] still fail the job.
[codex] 
[codex] Trivy package evidence is not a lifecycle authority and does not guarantee that
[codex] an image exposes its primary application version. The coverage report records
[codex] known Redis, Temurin, and controller-binary inventory limitations. Never infer a
[codex] Redis patch or Java CPU level from the broad source tag or from a successful OS
[codex] package scan.
[codex] 
[codex] ## Failure triage
[codex] 
[codex] - **Configuration error:** reproduce with the pinned validator version. Treat
[codex]   warnings and migrations as failures; correct the preset or repository config.
[codex] - **No extraction:** check the owning file's native manager pattern or adjacent
[codex]   annotation and compare debug logs. Do not seed the historical expected version
[codex]   into configuration.
[codex] - **No lookup or wrong package:** verify the real datasource identity, chart
[codex]   name, registry URL, tag prefix, build suffix, and flavor suffix. Record an
[codex]   unresolved standard-tool gap instead of adding a custom crawler.
[codex] - **Authentication or resolution failure:** preserve the failure. Fix encrypted
[codex]   Maven/registry access in the supported trust boundary; do not use Maven Local,
[codex]   drop internal dependencies, or swallow the error.
[codex] - **Finding without an update:** retain the Dependabot/scanner finding and route
[codex]   inherited or transitive remediation to the owning service. An update pull
[codex]   request is not proof that an advisory was detected.
[codex] - **CI failure on a bot branch:** determine whether the proposal needs its
[codex]   documented checksum, chart rendering, ARM64, state migration, or cross-repo
[codex]   companion review. Do not relax a guardrail or create orchestration drift.
[codex] - **Scanner database/download failure:** report the job as failed separately
[codex]   from vulnerability findings. Never turn an unavailable scan into a clean result.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate discovery and vulnerability scanners do not comprehensively establish
[codex] end-of-life status. Owners must still perform a quarterly support-policy review
[codex] against upstream lifecycle sources.

[codex] ## Phase 1 pilot evidence
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate `44.65.5` was initially run under Node `24.13.0` and rerun under the
[codex] workspace baseline Node `24.20.0` against a plain copy of the checkout. The
[codex] unpublished shared preset and repository configuration were merged in memory,
[codex] repository config discovery was suppressed, and local platform dry-run mode
[codex] was used with debug logging. This avoids resolving the not-yet-published GitHub
[codex] preset and includes newly created, untracked files.
[codex] 
[codex] The final extraction rerun found 98 occurrences in 34 package files:
[codex] 
[codex] | Manager | Files | Occurrences | Evidence |
[codex] | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
[codex] | Dockerfile | 1 | 1 | `nginx/Dockerfile.prod-smoke-assets` -> `alpine` |
[codex] | GitHub Actions | 3 | 11 | Both existing workflows plus the new validator workflow; checkout, setup-node, Node input, and runner identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Helm values | 2 | 13 | Kyverno digest overrides and five kube-prometheus-stack image identities were recognized. |
[codex] | Kubernetes | 11 | 29 | Stateful infrastructure, Jaeger, service init images, gateway images, local first-party images, and Kubernetes API kinds were recognized. |
[codex] | Regex | 17 | 44 | Shell/Tilt chart pins, tool releases, Kind, Kiali, inline Temurin, probe images, Playwright, and the Renovate validator were recognized. |
[codex] 
[codex] Three of the GitHub Actions occurrences come from the manual hosted-dry-run job
[codex] and repeat already-covered runner, setup-node, and Node identities; they do not
[codex] add a new dependency surface.
[codex] 
[codex] The first lookup run completed in about 34 seconds and reported 57 distinct
[codex] dependency records, 31 outdated records, and 104 candidate branches before
[codex] routine limits and dashboard approvals. Live lookups succeeded for all six
[codex] configured Helm repositories, npm, and most container registries. The final
[codex] rerun completed lookup and returned 101 candidate branches, with the expected
[codex] missing-GitHub-token warning and an anonymous Docker token warning. Registry
[codex] lookup failures are retained below instead of being presented as a clean scan.
[codex] 
[codex] Renovate's documented local platform supports `extract` and `lookup`, not a
[codex] true `full` dry run. Passing `--dry-run=full` falls back to lookup behavior.
[codex] Therefore extraction and live lookup are demonstrated locally, but branch-file
[codex] mutation and the published preset resolution still require a no-write hosted
[codex] observation after publication. No GitHub token was available in this worker,
[codex] by design, so GitHub-backed identities were extracted with
[codex] `github-token-required` and were not looked up. Those lookups are deferred to
[codex] the user-triggered Phase 12 job, which receives its ephemeral read-only token
[codex] inside GitHub Actions.

[codex]   or missing.

[codex] Choose scripts by runtime boundary:
[codex]

[codex] ## Bootstrap
[codex] 
[codex] - `bootstrap/install-verified-tool.sh` installs repo-pinned `kubectl`, Helm,
[codex]   Tilt, `mkcert`, Kind, `kubeconform`, `kube-linter`, and `kyverno` releases
[codex]   after verifying checked-in SHA-256 values.
[codex] - `bootstrap/check-tilt-prerequisites.sh` validates local tools, pinned binary
[codex]   versions, the host-published public ingress CA, DNS, Docker/Kind
[codex]   prerequisites, inotify budgets, pinned Gateway API and Calico state, and
[codex]   optional runtime security state. It reports drift and install commands
[codex]   without performing interactive cluster changes.
[codex] - `bootstrap/check-infra-tls-secrets.sh` is the focused read-only post-check
[codex]   used by `setup.sh` and Tilt. Tilt reruns the host-only
[codex]   `bootstrap/setup-infra-tls.sh` before PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ start
[codex]   so namespace recreation cannot leave the infrastructure TLS secrets missing.
[codex] - `bootstrap/reconcile-kind-inotify-budget.sh` raises low Kind node inotify
[codex]   values used by Kubernetes log-follow streams. Tilt runs it as
[codex]   `kind-node-inotify-budget` on every `tilt up` before workload resources
[codex]   start.
[codex] - `bootstrap/install-calico.sh` installs or reconciles pinned Calico CNI for
[codex]   Kind clusters created with `disableDefaultCNI`. It also uses the inotify
[codex]   reconciliation helper. A live `docker exec kind-control-plane sysctl ...`
[codex]   recovery command is diagnostic only; use the helper or Tilt resource for the
[codex]   durable local fix.
[codex] - `bootstrap/setup-k8s-tls.sh` and `bootstrap/setup-infra-tls.sh` are host-only
[codex]   certificate bootstrap scripts. Do not run them from an AI container because
[codex]   the browser must trust the host mkcert CA. `setup-k8s-tls.sh` fails closed
[codex]   unless the target is the host `kind-kind` context backed by the `kind`
[codex]   cluster, then atomically publishes only the public mkcert root at
[codex]   `nginx/certs/k8s/_mkcert-rootCA.pem` for the workspace lazy-trust command.
[codex]   The publication remains ignored by Git; no CA private key is published.
[codex] 
[codex] Use `../setup.sh` when you want the full local bootstrap to converge
[codex] repo-managed prerequisites and recreate the local Kind cluster. Use
[codex] `bootstrap/install-verified-tool.sh` for a single pinned binary, and use
[codex] `bootstrap/check-tilt-prerequisites.sh` as a read-only report before or after
[codex] setup.
[codex]

[codex]

[codex]   side-by-side workspace checkout because Tiltfile evaluation references
[codex]   sibling service repositories.

[codex]   kube-linter, Kyverno fixtures, generated local Tilt-tag admission replay, a
[codex]   rendered production Kyverno Helm check that rejects mutable controller/hook
[codex]   image refs, image pinning, secrets-only checks, namespace PSA checks, and
[codex]   active setup guidance scans. It also rejects Jaeger/Kiali public-entry drift
[codex]   in checked-in manifests and keeps the Kiali auth contract plus the Jaeger
[codex]   internal-only storage/service contract pinned in static review. Its
[codex]   kubeconform pass validates checked-in Kubernetes resource manifests, skips
[codex]   Kustomize patch fragments under `patches/` directories and the schema-v2
[codex]   production desired-state manifest as a standalone Kubernetes resource, and
[codex]   validates the rendered production app and infrastructure overlays that
[codex]   consume the Kubernetes inputs.

[codex]   `kubernetes/production/apps`, `kubernetes/production/infrastructure`, and the
[codex]   reviewed production route/ingress/monitoring/egress output, verifies
[codex]   the digest-pinned GHCR image inventory, rejects local `:latest` /
[codex]   `:tilt-` image paths, localhost hosts, placeholder Auth0 hosts, and
[codex]   `imagePullPolicy: Never`, rejects rendered observability Ingress/HTTPRoute/
[codex]   Gateway exposure for Grafana, Prometheus, Jaeger, and Kiali, uses a live
[codex]   Helm server-side dry run for the production Kiali render so namespace-scoped
[codex]   RBAC is fully reviewed, verifies the Redis StatefulSet uses a `5Gi`
[codex]   `redis-data` claim template, and applies the production image Kyverno policy
[codex]   to the rendered app overlay.

[codex] ## Orchestration Workflows
[codex] 
[codex] Dependency update pull-request ownership, activation, cost constraints, and
[codex] failure triage live in [Dependency Automation](dependency-automation.md). The
[codex] focused `dependency-automation-config.yml` workflow runs Renovate's official
[codex] strict configuration validator against the repository config and shared preset;
[codex] it does not install the App or open dependency pull requests.
[codex] 
[codex] The weekly/manual `exact-image-security-evidence.yml` workflow renders the
[codex] checked-in production/controller sources offline, resolves each rendered ref to
[codex] an exact platform digest, and publishes Trivy inventories and vulnerability
[codex] reports. Its operating boundary, artifact contents, and known coverage gaps are
[codex] owned by [Dependency Automation](dependency-automation.md#exact-image-security-evidence).
[codex] 
[codex] ### `security-guardrails.yml`
[codex] 
[codex] The orchestration repo now has a dedicated static security workflow for the
[codex] manifest guardrail suite. It is intentionally additive beside `test-setup.yml`;
[codex] it does not reuse the stale DinD suites as current security guardrails.
[codex] 
[codex] It now runs on every push to `main` and every pull request targeting `main`.
[codex] The narrower path filter was removed so guarded security surfaces cannot bypass
[codex] the workflow when a new file path is added to the static scope.
[codex]
